FastMDXplora (**F**ully **A**utomated **Sy**s**T**em for **M**olecular **D**ynamics e**Xplora**tion) is a project-level orchestrator designed to automate end-to-end molecular dynamics (MD) studies [src/fastmdxplora/__init__.py:1-6, docs/index.md:1-3](). Given a structure file or a 4-character PDB code, the software handles system preparation, production simulation, trajectory analysis, and deliverable report generation within a unified framework [README.md:31-37](). 

This page provides a high-level overview of the FastMDXplora architecture, pipeline structure, repository layout, and core design principles.

```mermaid
graph TD
    UserInput["User Input (PDB Code / Config / GUI)"] --> Orchestrator["FastMDXplora (src/fastmdxplora/orchestrator.py)"]
    Orchestrator --> SetupPhase["Setup Phase (fastmdxplora.setup)"]
    SetupPhase --> SimPhase["Simulation Phase (fastmdxplora.simulation)"]
    SimPhase --> AnalPhase["Analysis Phase (fastmdxplora.analysis)"]
    AnalPhase --> ReportPhase["Report Phase (fastmdxplora.report)"]
    ReportPhase --> ManifestOutput["Manifest & Deliverables (manifest.json)"]
```
*Figure 1: High-level architectural pipeline mapping user inputs and phase orchestration to code modules.*

Sources: `[src/fastmdxplora/__init__.py:1-6](), [docs/index.md:1-3](), [README.md:31-37](), [src/fastmdxplora/__init__.py:104-105]()`

---

## High-Level Architecture and Repository Layout

FastMDXplora organizes its codebase into modular functional units under `src/fastmdxplora/`, separating orchestrators, phase pipelines, client interfaces, and validation components [STRUCTURE.md:4-32](). 

```mermaid
graph TD
    Root["FastMDXplora / src / fastmdxplora"] --> Orchestration["orchestrator.py & runs_here.py"]
    Root --> SetupSub["setup/ (pipeline.py, pdbfix.py, ligand.py)"]
    Root --> SimSub["simulation/ (pipeline.py, runner.py)"]
    Root --> AnalSub["analysis/ (orchestrator, trajectory loading)"]
    Root --> RepSub["report/ (document, slides, deposition)"]
    Root --> Interfaces["cli/main.py, gui/, mcp/, agent/"]
    Root --> Infra["provenance.py, refusals.py, dependencies.py"]
```
*Figure 2: Core repository structure mapping directory modules to system components.*

Sources: `[STRUCTURE.md:4-32]()`

---

## Core Philosophy and Design Tenets

FastMDXplora is built on strict determinism and refusal-driven safety. Rather than guessing ambiguous parameters (such as protonation states or missing residue patches), subsystems raise explicit refusals to prevent silent scientific errors [README.md:69-74](). Every study is fully declared via a configuration schema (`resolved_config.yml`) and completely recorded via an execution manifest (`manifest.json`), ensuring absolute reproducibility across local workstations and compute clusters [README.md:76-94]().

Sources: `[README.md:69-94]()`

## Purpose and Scope
This section covers the complete installation and initial execution lifecycle of FastMDXplora. It details the recommended `conda-forge` distribution [docs/installation.md:3-24](), granular `pip` optional dependencies [pyproject.toml:87-160](), reproducible development environments via `environment.yml`, containerized deployments using Apptainer/Docker [.github/workflows/container.yml:28-142](), environment inspection through `fastmdx info` [README.md:52-56](), and the first study walkthrough [README.md:26-37]().

Sources: [README.md:26-57](), [pyproject.toml:64-160](), [docs/installation.md:1-122](), [.github/workflows/container.yml:28-142]()

---

## Installation Pathways: Conda-Forge vs PyPI
FastMDXplora relies on heavy scientific packages for molecular mechanics (`openmm`), structural repair (`pdbfixer`), small-molecule charging (`openff-toolkit`, `ambertools`, `rdkit`, `propka`), and enhanced sampling (`openmm-plumed`) [recipes/fastmdxplora/recipe.yaml:40-94](). Because several critical dependencies lack PyPI binary distributions (specifically `openff-toolkit` dependencies and `openmm-plumed`), `conda-forge` is the primary recommended distribution channel [docs/installation.md:14-17]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    User["User Workspace"] -->|Prefers conda-forge| CondaPath["conda create -n fastmdxplora -c conda-forge fastmdxplora"]
    User -->|Prefers pip| PipPath["pip install fastmdxplora"]
    
    CondaPath --> FullStack["Full Pipeline: Setup, MD, Ligands, Plumed, PDF"]
    PipPath --> PartialStack["Core Analysis & Reporting Only"]
    
    PartialStack --> ExtraMD["pip install fastmdxplora[md]"]
    PartialStack --> ExtraLigand["pip install fastmdxplora[ligand]"]
    
    ExtraLigand --> CondaBridge["conda install -c conda-forge openff-toolkit ambertools"]
    
    subgraph "Code Entities"
    CondaPath --> RC["recipes/fastmdxplora/recipe.yaml"]
    PipPath --> PT["pyproject.toml"]
    end
```
*Figure 1: Installation Routing bridging user installation choices to package manager specifications (`pyproject.toml` and `recipe.yaml`).*

Sources: [pyproject.toml:64-160](), [recipes/fastmdxplora/recipe.yaml:40-94](), [docs/installation.md:3-65]()

### Pip Optional Dependencies Matrix
When installing via `pip`, capabilities are partitioned into optional extras defined in `pyproject.toml`:

| Extra Name | Target Functionality | Included Packages | Source / Note |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `[md]` | Setup and Simulation | `pdbfixer`, `openmm >=8.2` | Requires OpenMM wheel availability [pyproject.toml:101-108]() |
| `[ligand]` | Small molecule prep | `openmmforcefields`, `rdkit`, `propka` | Requires external `conda-forge` for `openff-toolkit` & `ambertools` [docs/installation.md:43-48]() |
| `[pdf]` | Publication PDF reports | `weasyprint >=60` | Requires system libraries `libpango`, `libcairo` [docs/installation.md:56-61]() |
| `[amber]` | Fast AMBER trajectory reading | `netCDF4 >=1.6` | Speeds up trajectory parsing via `netCDF4` [pyproject.toml:128-132]() |
| `[umap]` | Dimensionality reduction | `umap-learn >=0.5` | Optional projection space algorithm [pyproject.toml:133-137]() |
| `[movies]` | Browser-based frame rendering | `playwright >=1.40` | Requires `playwright install chromium` [docs/installation.md:118-120]() |

Sources: [pyproject.toml:87-160](), [docs/installation.md:27-64]()

---

## Environment Configuration and Developer Setup
For developers modifying the FastMDXplora source tree, the repository provides a complete conda environment definition file (`environment.yml`) containing all necessary binary dependencies and scientific stacks [docs/installation.md:68-77]().

```bash
git clone https://github.com/aai-research-lab/FastMDXplora.git
cd FastMDXplora
conda env create -f environment.yml
conda activate fastmdxplora
pip install -e ".[dev]"
pytest -q
```

The test suite validates dependency declarations automatically to ensure that no module is imported without a corresponding declaration in `pyproject.toml` or conda manifests [tests/test_dependencies_declared.py:1-11]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    EnvYml["environment.yml"] --> Micromamba["mamba-org/setup-micromamba"]
    Micromamba --> CondaEnv["conda environment: fastmdxplora"]
    CondaEnv --> EditableInstall["pip install -e . --no-deps"]
    EditableInstall --> CLIEntryPoint["fastmdx (fastmdxplora.cli.main:main)"]
    
    subgraph "Verification Code"
    CLIEntryPoint --> TestParser["tests/test_docs_examples.py::_build_parser"]
    CLIEntryPoint --> TestDeps["tests/test_dependencies_declared.py::_imported_distributions"]
    end
```
*Figure 2: Development bootstrap and validation flow connecting `environment.yml` to CLI entry points (`fastmdxplora.cli.main:main`) and test suites (`tests/test_docs_examples.py`).*

Sources: [recipes/fastmdxplora/recipe.yaml:31-39](), [tests/test_docs_examples.py:15-65](), [tests/test_dependencies_declared.py:1-45](), [docs/installation.md:68-96]()

---

## Container Images and Cluster Execution
For high-performance computing clusters or environments without direct `conda-forge` network access, FastMDXplora provides automated container build pipelines for Apptainer (`.sif`) and Docker [container/fastmdx.def](), [.github/workflows/container.yml:1-35]().

The workflow automatically validates that the specified version is indexed on `conda-forge` before invoking `apptainer build --fakeroot` against `container/fastmdx.def` [.github/workflows/container.yml:68-142]().

```bash
# Building an Apptainer image manually from the definition file
apptainer build --fakeroot fastmdx-2.6.0.sif container/fastmdx.def

# Running an explore workflow inside the container
apptainer exec --nv fastmdx-2.6.0.sif fastmdx explore --system 181L
```

Sources: [.github/workflows/container.yml:28-142](), [container/fastmdx.def:1-50]()

---

## Environment Inspection and Backends: `fastmdx info`
To verify that all simulation platforms, force fields, analysis toolkits, and reporting binaries are correctly bound, use the built-in diagnostic command:

```bash
fastmdx info
```

This command interrogates the active Python runtime, probes OpenMM platforms (`CUDA`, `OpenCL`, `CPU`, `Reference`), checks small-molecule parameterization backends (`ambertools`, `openff-toolkit`), and checks PDF rendering dependencies (`weasyprint`), printing missing dependencies along with precise installation instructions [README.md:52-56](), [docs/installation.md:124-134]().

Sources: [README.md:52-56](), [docs/installation.md:124-134]()

---

## First Study Walkthrough and Demo Execution
A first study can be executed immediately via the command-line interface or the local GUI dashboard. 

### 1. Command-Line Exploration
The simplest end-to-end command fetches T4 lysozyme (`181L`), parameterizes the bound benzene ligand, runs minimization and production MD, calculates structural properties, and compiles a comprehensive PDF report [README.md:26-37](), [tests/test_docs_examples.py:20-38]():

```bash
fastmdx explore --system 181L
```

### 2. Graphical Dashboard Walkthrough
To launch the localhost zero-dependency interactive dashboard for study configuration and live telemetry tracking [README.md:39-43](), [docs/index.md:10-16]():

```bash
fastmdx gui
```

This starts a local Tornado/HTTP dashboard server where users can input a PDB code (e.g., `1L2Y`), inspect phase configuration schemas, adjust production step counts, monitor live GPU telemetry, and render Mol* molecular viewer scenes.

Sources: [README.md:26-44](), [docs/index.md:10-18](), [tests/test_docs_examples.py:20-47]()

## Purpose and Scope
This page defines the foundational data structures, execution lifecycles, and design philosophies underpinning FastMDXplora. It details how studies are structured, how configurations are frozen into `resolved_config.yml`, how runs report their history via `manifest.json` and provenance records, and how the **refusal philosophy** prevents invalid scientific claims across all subsystems.

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/batch/explorer.py:1-38`, `src/fastmdxplora/orchestrator.py:1-174`, `src/fastmdxplora/refusals.py:1-57`

---

## 1. Study Lifecycle and Output Layout

FastMDXplora unifies single-run execution and multi-system parameter sweeps under a single execution path managed by `BatchExplorer` (`src/fastmdxplora/batch/explorer.py:1-6`). There is no separate "single run" path; a single-system configuration is simply treated as a batch of one (`src/fastmdxplora/batch/explorer.py:3-6`).

The output layout adapts dynamically to the run count (`src/fastmdxplora/batch/explorer.py:8-15`):
- **One run**: A flat, direct layout written to the target output directory containing `output/setup/`, `output/simulation/`, `output/analysis/`, `output/report/`, accompanied by `manifest.json` and `resolved_config.yml`. No `runs/` wrapper or `batch_manifest.json` is generated.
- **Many runs**: Each run is isolated in `output/runs/<id>/` as a complete, independent study directory, indexed by a top-level `batch_manifest.json`.

Every run executes sequentially through the canonical phase sequence defined in `PHASES` (`src/fastmdxplora/orchestrator.py:58`):
1. `setup`: System preparation, protonation, and force field application.
2. `simulation`: OpenMM-backed runner execution, equilibration, and production sampling.
3. `analysis`: Trajectory parsing, statistical evaluations, and structural measurements.
4. `report`: Methods prose generation, statistical validation, and report bundling.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph NaturalLanguageSpace ["Natural Language / User Input"]
        CLI["CLI Command: fastmdx explore"]
        UserConfig["User Config YAML File"]
    end

    subgraph CodeEntitySpace ["Code Entity Space"]
        MainCLI["fastmdxplora.cli.main.main"] --> Validate["fastmdxplora.config.validate_config"]
        Validate --> Explorer["fastmdxplora.batch.explorer.BatchExplorer"]
        Explorer --> SingleOrBatch{Is Multi-Run Sweep?}
        
        SingleOrBatch -- No --> FlatRun["Flat Directory Layout (manifest.json, resolved_config.yml)"]
        SingleOrBatch -- Yes --> RunsWrapper["output/runs/<id>/ + batch_manifest.json"]

        Explorer --> Orchestrator["fastmdxplora.orchestrator.FastMDXplora"]
        Orchestrator --> PhaseSeq["PHASES: setup -> simulation -> analysis -> report"]
        PhaseSeq --> PhaseRunner["fastmdxplora.orchestrator.PhaseResult"]
    end

    CLI --> MainCLI
    UserConfig --> Validate

    classDef default fill:#fff,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px;
```
*Figure 1: Bridging user invocation space to the core orchestration pipeline.*

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/batch/explorer.py:1-38`, `src/fastmdxplora/orchestrator.py:1-60`, `tests/test_cli.py:124-133`

---

## 2. Resolved Configuration (`resolved_config.yml`)

Before any study phase executes, raw user configurations undergo strict validation against the schema registry (`src/fastmdxplora/config/`) and normalization. Once validated, the final effective configuration—incorporating all default values, merged overrides, and sweep expansions—is serialized to `resolved_config.yml` in the run directory.

This file guarantees reproducibility by capturing the absolute state of all parameters (force field choices, step counts, restraint constants, and solvent padding) without relying on transient CLI arguments or user memory.

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/batch/explorer.py:1-16`, `src/fastmdxplora/config/__init__.py`

---

## 3. Manifest (`manifest.json`) and Provenance Records

Each completed or errored run produces a `manifest.json` file. The manifest acts as the machine-readable ledger of the study, aggregating `PhaseResult` and `RunResult` records (`src/fastmdxplora/orchestrator.py:95-174`).

### Provenance Tracking
To ensure complete reproducibility, FastMDXplora captures two orthogonal dimensions of provenance via `src/fastmdxplora/provenance.py`:
1. **Source Provenance (`source_provenance`)**: Inspects the package's underlying git checkout (walking up from the package path rather than the working directory) to record the exact git commit hash, branch, and a `dirty` flag indicating whether uncommitted modifications were present (`src/fastmdxplora/provenance.py:55-128`).
2. **Structure Provenance (`structure_provenance`)**: Computes cryptographic hashes and metadata digests of input PDB/CIF files so that structural inputs remain uniquely identifiable even if source files are moved or renamed (`src/fastmdxplora/provenance.py:158-172`).

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph NaturalLanguageSpace ["Artifact Origin Space"]
        SourceRepo["Source Code Checkout (.git)"]
        RawPDB["Input Structure File (PDB/CIF)"]
    end

    subgraph CodeEntitySpace ["Code Entity Space"]
        ProvMod["fastmdxplora.provenance"]
        SrcProv["source_provenance() -> {'commit': str, 'dirty': bool}"]
        StrProv["structure_provenance() -> hash & metadata digest"]
        
        Orchestrator["fastmdxplora.orchestrator.FastMDXplora"] --> PhaseRes["PhaseResult.to_dict()"]
        SrcProv --> Manifest["manifest.json"]
        StrProv --> Manifest
        PhaseRes --> Manifest
    end

    SourceRepo --> ProvMod
    RawPDB --> ProvMod
    ProvMod --> SrcProv
    ProvMod --> StrProv

    classDef default fill:#fff,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px;
```
*Figure 2: Provenance aggregation flowing from physical inputs and source code checkpoints into the structured manifest.*

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/orchestrator.py:95-174`, `src/fastmdxplora/provenance.py:55-172`, `src/fastmdxplora/provenance.py:105-128`

---

## 4. The Refusal Philosophy

Every subsystem in FastMDXplora is governed by an explicit **refusal philosophy**: when a study lacks sufficient biological definition, proper input parameters, or statistical sampling, the software stops immediately and explains why, rather than generating plausible but incorrect numerical outputs (`docs/refusals.md:3-7`).

### Core Principle
> **The validator may say what the schema permits. It may never say what the chemistry requires.** (`docs/refusals.md:96-97`)

### The Four Refusal Kinds
Refusals are classified into four distinct categories (`src/fastmdxplora/refusals.py:94-123`) to dictate who or what can resolve the issue:

| Kind | Meaning | Remedy |
|---|---|---|
| `structural` | The configuration violates schema constraints or omits required fields | Correct the configuration and retry (`docs/refusals.md:76`) |
| `semantic` | The study is well-formed, but the biological system is under-determined (e.g., ambiguous protonation states) | Make a scientific decision about the system (`docs/refusals.md:77`) |
| `environmental` | A required backend (such as OpenMM or PDBFixer) or service is missing | Fix the environment or machine setup (`docs/refusals.md:78`) |
| `insufficient` | The study is sound, but collected trajectory data is statistically insufficient to support the requested claim | Perform additional sampling (`docs/refusals.md:79`) |

### Disclosure Levels
To prevent automated agents or programmatic callers from guessing scientific parameters while allowing configuration corrections, each refusal specifies a disclosure level (`src/fastmdxplora.refusals.Disclosure`):
- `permitted_values`: The complete legal set is known and may be disclosed (e.g., valid box shapes) (`src/fastmdxplora/refusals.py:140-141`).
- `field_only`: The offending setting may be named, but no value may be suggested (`src/fastmdxplora/refusals.py:143-145`).
- `action`: An exact non-scientific remedy exists, such as an installation command (`src/fastmdxplora/refusals.py:147-149`).
- `nothing`: The software does not possess the chemical answer and refuses to guess (`src/fastmdxplora/refusals.py:151-152`).

Programmatic callers can inspect refusals uniformly using `refusal_of()` (`docs/refusals.md:22-35`), which wraps any standard exception into a structured `Refusal` object containing a hierarchical dot-separated code (`<phase>.<family>.<what>`) (`docs/refusals.md:47`).

Sources: `docs/refusals.md:1-187`, `src/fastmdxplora/refusals.py:1-154`, `src/fastmdxplora/refusals.py:94-123`

---

# Orchestration and Configuration

This section provides an overview of how molecular dynamics studies are declared through structured configurations, validated against rigorous schemas, exposed via a rich command-line interface (CLI), and driven through sequential or batch exploration phases by the core orchestrator. 

As a parent page, this document outlines the high-level architecture and relationships between configuration management, command-line verbs, and batch orchestration campaigns. For deep technical details, refer to the child pages:
- Configuration System and Schema: [Configuration System and Schema](#2.1)
- Command Line Interface: [Command Line Interface](#2.2)
- Orchestrator and Batch Campaigns: [Orchestrator and Batch Campaigns](#2.3)

---

## 2.1. Configuration System and Schema

Declarative configuration files (`.yml`) specify all parameters required to drive a study across its scientific lifecycle. The configuration architecture relies on a registry system defined in `schema.py` (see [STRUCTURE.md: src/fastmdxplora/](STRUCTURE.md)()), which manages `Field` and `PhaseSchema` definitions. The config loader normalizes user inputs, applies intelligent defaults, supports template generation, and detects setting diffs.

The configuration system enforces strict schema validation using `validate_config` [src/fastmdxplora/batch/explorer.py:61-61] and `load_config_file` [src/fastmdxplora/batch/explorer.py:61-61]. Every parameter is bound to a specific phase (`setup`, `simulation`, `analysis`, `report`, or `execution`), ensuring that ill-formed entries or unrecognized keys are immediately rejected rather than silently ignored.

For comprehensive documentation on schema registries, field normalization, template generation, diffing, and type definitions, see [Configuration System and Schema](#2.1).

```mermaid
graph TD
    UserConfig["User Config File (.yml)"] -->|load_config_file| Loader[fastmdxplora.config]
    Loader -->|validate_config| SchemaRegistry["schema.py Registry"]
    SchemaRegistry -->|Normalized Settings| ResolvedConfig["resolved_config.yml"]
    SchemaRegistry -->|Expanded Runs| BatchExplorer["fastmdxplora.batch.explorer.BatchExplorer"]

    classDef default fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px;
    class UserConfig,Loader,SchemaRegistry,ResolvedConfig,BatchExplorer default;
```
*Figure 1: Configuration loading, validation, and schema resolution flow mapping user input files to internal execution structures.*

**Sources:** `src/fastmdxplora/batch/explorer.py:61-61`, `STRUCTURE.md:1-89`

---

## 2.2. Command Line Interface

The command-line interface (`fastmdx` or `fastmdxplora`, implemented in `src/fastmdxplora/cli/main.py`) exposes all configuration options as schema-derived command flags. Every CLI verb corresponds to a core pipeline action or utility:

| Verb / Subcommand | Target Code / Role | Description |
|-------------------|--------------------|-------------|
| `explore` / `xplore` | `FastMDXplora` | Runs the full pipeline (`setup` → `simulation` → `analysis` → `report`) [src/fastmdxplora/cli/main.py:6-6] |
| `setup` | `fastmdxplora.setup.pipeline` | Prepares the molecular system (PDB fix, protonation, solvation, ionization) [src/fastmdxplora/cli/main.py:7-7] |
| `simulate` | `fastmdxplora.simulation.runner` | Executes OpenMM-backed molecular dynamics stages [src/fastmdxplora/cli/main.py:8-8] |
| `analyze` | `fastmdxplora.analysis` | Computes structural, energetic, and dynamic trajectories properties [src/fastmdxplora/cli/main.py:9-9] |
| `report` | `fastmdxplora.report` | Generates summary documents, statistics, and publication assets [src/fastmdxplora/cli/main.py:10-10] |
| `agent` | `fastmdxplora.agent` | Natural language study generation and proposal loops [docs/cli.md:28-28] |
| `gui` | `fastmdxplora.gui` | Serves the dependency-free localhost dashboard [docs/cli.md:29-29] |
| `mcp` | `fastmdxplora.mcp` | Model Context Protocol server for AI application integration [docs/cli.md:30-30] |

Flags are dynamically derived from phase schemas, allowing fine-grained control via prefixed arguments (e.g., `--setup-ph`, `--simulate-duration-ns`) [src/fastmdxplora/cli/main.py:14-18]. 

For detailed command references, argument parsing rules, and defaults files, see [Command Line Interface](#2.2).

```mermaid
graph TD
    CLI["CLI Command: fastmdx.cli.main.main"] -->|Subcommand Router| Explore["explore / xplore"]
    CLI -->|Subcommand Router| Setup["setup"]
    CLI -->|Subcommand Router| Sim["simulate"]
    CLI -->|Subcommand Router| Gui["gui"]
    
    Explore -->|Invokes| Orchestrator["fastmdxplora.orchestrator.FastMDXplora"]
    Setup -->|Invokes| SetupPipeline["fastmdxplora.setup.pipeline.run"]
    Sim -->|Invokes| SimRunner["fastmdxplora.simulation.runner.run_simulation"]
    Gui -->|Invokes| DashboardServer["fastmdxplora.gui.server._DashboardServer"]

    classDef default fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px;
    class CLI,Explore,Setup,Sim,Gui,Orchestrator,SetupPipeline,SimRunner,DashboardServer default;
```
*Figure 2: CLI execution routing mapping natural language command-line verbs to underlying Python entry points and pipeline modules.*

**Sources:** `src/fastmdxplora/cli/main.py:1-45`, `docs/cli.md:18-39`

---

## 2.3. Orchestrator and Batch Campaigns

The project-level orchestrator (`FastMDXplora` in `src/fastmdxplora/orchestrator.py`) manages shared state, registered phases (`PHASES = ("setup", "simulation", "analysis", "report")`) [src/fastmdxplora/orchestrator.py:58-58], and sequential execution. 

Every study—whether a single system or a massive parameter sweep—is handled uniformly through `BatchExplorer` [src/fastmdxplora/batch/explorer.py:1-4]:
- **Single run:** Writes flat outputs directly to the target directory alongside `manifest.json` and `resolved_config.yml` [src/fastmdxplora/batch/explorer.py:11-13].
- **Batch campaigns:** Expands parameter sweeps across multiple systems, storing each individual study under `output/runs/<id>/` indexed by a top-level `batch_manifest.json` [src/fastmdxplora/batch/explorer.py:14-15].

Execution modes support sequential processing or parallel process pools with device pinning (`devices: [0, 1, ...]`) for multi-GPU hardware distribution [src/fastmdxplora/batch/explorer.py:17-23]. Each phase records lightweight status objects (`PhaseResult` and `RunResult`) capturing execution artifacts, timing, and refusal states [src/fastmdxplora/orchestrator.py:95-174].

For full details on phase progression, run results, process pool execution, and GPU sharing, see [Orchestrator and Batch Campaigns](#2.3).

**Sources:** `src/fastmdxplora/batch/explorer.py:1-38`, `src/fastmdxplora/orchestrator.py:1-60`

---

## Purpose and Scope

The FastMDXplora configuration system acts as the single source of truth for the entire study configuration surface. Every parameter a user can specify—whether project-level (`output`, `include`/`exclude`, `verbose`) or phase-specific (`setup`, `simulation`, `analysis`, `report`)—is declared in a centralized schema registry. Four major subsystems read directly from this registry to prevent drift: strict validation loaders, YAML template generators, resolved-config dumpers for provenance, and static documentation validators.

Sources: `[src/fastmdxplora/config/schema.py:1-25]`, `[src/fastmdxplora/config/loader.py:1-23]`, `[src/fastmdxplora/config/generate.py:1-14]()`

---

## The Schema Registry (`schema.py`)

The core of the schema system is defined in `[src/fastmdxplora/config/schema.py:1-155]()`. It centers around two primary dataclasses: `Field` and `PhaseSchema`.

- **`Field`**: Represents a single configurable option. It tracks attributes including `name`, `type`, `default`, `help`, `example`, `choices`, numeric bounds (`minimum`, `maximum`), and `phase_sentinel`. The `phase_sentinel` attribute allows an option's effective user-facing default to differ from the internal phase initialization value (e.g., `pressure_bar` defaulting to 1 bar while initializing as `None` to detect explicit user overrides via `pressure_atm`) [src/fastmdxplora/config/schema.py:80-143]().
- **`PhaseSchema`**: Groups an ordered tuple of `Field` objects together with a phase `name` and `description` [src/fastmdxplora/config/schema.py:145-155]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    sub5["Natural Language Space"]
    NL1["User YAML Config"] --> NL2["CLI Flags"]
    NL2 --> NL3["GUI Builder"]

    sub6["Code Entity Space"]
    NL1 -->|Parsed by| L1["fastmdxplora.config.loader.load_config_file"]
    NL2 -->|Parsed by| L2["fastmdxplora.cli.main"]
    NL3 -->|Rendered by| L3["fastmdxplora.gui.config_builder"]

    L1 --> S["fastmdxplora.config.schema.PHASE_SCHEMAS"]
    L2 --> S
    L3 --> S

    S -->|Validation| V["fastmdxplora.config.loader.validate_config"]
    S -->|Templates| T["fastmdxplora.config.generate.generate_template"]
    S -->|Export| D["fastmdxplora.config.generate.write_resolved_config"]

    style sub5 fill:none,stroke:none
    style sub6 fill:none,stroke:none
```

Sources: `[src/fastmdxplora/config/schema.py:1-155]()`

---

## Loading, Validation, and Normalization (`loader.py`)

Configuration files are ingested through `load_config_file()` in `[src/fastmdxplora/config/loader.py:50-91]()`. The loading pipeline performs strict validation to prevent silent failures caused by typos or invalid types [src/fastmdxplora/config/loader.py:7-14]().

### Validation Workflow

1. **Top-Level and Phase-Level Checks**: Validates that all keys present in the YAML mapping belong to recognized top-level properties or phase blocks (`setup`, `simulation`, `analysis`, `report`).
2. **Did-You-Mean Suggestions**: Unknown keys trigger `ConfigError` exceptions carrying fuzzy-match and case-insensitive suggestions via `_suggest()` and `_suggestion_only()` [src/fastmdxplora/config/loader.py:96-150]().
3. **Type Coercion**: `_check_type()` handles YAML parsing idiosyncrasies (e.g., permitting integer values for float fields like `temperature_K: 300` while strictly rejecting Python `bool` subclasses where numeric types are required) [src/fastmdxplora/config/loader.py:169-181]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["load_config_file(path)"] --> B["yaml.safe_load(fh)"]
    B --> C{Is Mapping?}
    C -- No --> D["Raise ConfigError (not_a_mapping)"]
    C -- Yes --> E["canonical_phase_keys(data)"]
    E --> F["normalise_config(data)"]
    F --> G["validate_config(data)"]
    G --> H{Unknown Keys?}
    H -- Yes --> I["Raise ConfigError with _suggest()"]
    H -- No --> J{Type Mismatch?}
    J -- Yes --> K["Raise ConfigError (type invalid)"]
    J -- No --> L["Return Validated Config Dict"]

    style A fill:none,stroke:none
    style L fill:none,stroke:none
```

Sources: `[src/fastmdxplora/config/loader.py:1-181]()`

---

## Template Generation and Resolved-Config Dumping (`generate.py`)

Template generation and reproducibility logs are managed by `[src/fastmdxplora/config/generate.py:1-173]()`.

- **Template Generation (`generate_template`)**: Powers the `fastmdx config` command [docs/config.md:12](). It programmatically loops through `TOP_LEVEL` and `PHASE_SCHEMAS`, formatting field defaults, examples, and help strings into a fully commented YAML file [src/fastmdxplora/config/generate.py:111-165](). Users can request a `minimal` layout or a comprehensive template where phase blocks are commented out by default [src/fastmdxplora/config/generate.py:111-124]().
- **Resolved-Config Dump (`write_resolved_config`)**: Upon executing a study, the fully merged configuration (comprising built-in defaults, loaded configuration file values, and explicit runtime overrides) is serialized to `resolved_config.yml` in the study output directory, ensuring complete auditability and reproducibility [docs/config.md:68]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    sub7["Natural Language Space"]
    N1["Command: fastmdx config -f study.yml"] --> N2["Completed Study Folder"]

    sub8["Code Entity Space"]
    N1 --> C1["fastmdxplora.config.generate.generate_template"]
    C1 --> O1["Generated YAML Template"]

    N2 --> C2["fastmdxplora.config.generate.write_resolved_config"]
    C2 --> O2["resolved_config.yml"]

    style sub7 fill:none,stroke:none
    style sub8 fill:none,stroke:none
```

Sources: `[src/fastmdxplora/config/generate.py:1-173]`, `[docs/config.md:12-21]`

---

## Phase Setting Types and Documentation Reference

To bridge runtime configuration parsing with static analysis and IDE tooling, FastMDXplora automatically maintains type definitions and consistency tests.

- **Phase Setting Types (`phase_settings_types.py`)**: Defines `TypedDict` structures (`SetupSettings`, `SimulateSettings`, `AnalyzeSettings`, `ReportSettings`) corresponding to each phase's configuration options [src/fastmdxplora/config/phase_settings_types.py:1-163]().
- **Documentation Integrity (`test_the_docs_are_honest.py`)**: Tests such as `TestEveryAnalysisIsDocumented` and `TestTheCollectiveVariablesAreAllNamed` inspect both the schema registry (`_REGISTRY`) and Markdown documentation files under `docs/` to guarantee that published counts, analyses, and collective variable lists never drift from codebase implementations [tests/validation/test_the_docs_are_honest.py:42-122]().

Sources: `[src/fastmdxplora/config/phase_settings_types.py:1-164]`, `[tests/validation/test_the_docs_are_honest.py:42-122]`

---

The Command Line Interface (CLI) serves as the primary terminal-based control plane for FastMDXplora, exposed via the console scripts `fastmdx` and `fastmdxplora` [docs/cli.md:13-14](). Its core responsibility is parsing command-line flags, mapping them into structured configuration dictionaries [src/fastmdxplora/cli/main.py:15-18](), and driving execution through the orchestrator.

---

## 1. CLI Entry Point and Argument Parser Architecture

The CLI is rooted in `src/fastmdxplora/__main__.py` [STRUCTURE.md:41-41](), which invokes the main entry point defined in `src/fastmdxplora/cli/main.py` [STRUCTURE.md:42-45](). Argument parsing is implemented using Python's standard `argparse` library, translating phase-specific option tuples (such as `_SETUP_OPTIONS` and `_SIMULATION_OPTIONS`) into command-line flags.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph NaturalLanguageSpace ["User Input & CLI Invocation"]
        A["Terminal Command: fastmdx explore --system 1UBQ"]
    end

    subgraph CodeEntitySpace ["Code Entity Space"]
        B["src/fastmdxplora/__main__.py"] -->|invokes| C["src/fastmdxplora/cli/main.py"]
        C -->|parses via| D["argparse.ArgumentParser"]
        D -->|maps options| E["src/fastmdxplora/orchestrator.py"]
    end

    A --> B

    style NaturalLanguageSpace fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style CodeEntitySpace fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
```
*Diagram 1: CLI execution flow bridging invocation to core orchestration.*

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/cli/main.py:1-45` [src/fastmdxplora/cli/main.py:1-45](), `STRUCTURE.md:41-45` [STRUCTURE.md:41-45]()

---

## 2. Command Verbs and Subcommands

FastMDXplora exposes a modular set of verbs. Each subcommand either drives a specific phase, inspects the environment, or launches external helper modes (such as GUI or MCP servers).

| Subcommand | Function / Purpose |
| :--- | :--- |
| `explore` / `xplore` | Run the full four-phase pipeline (`setup` $\rightarrow$ `simulation` $\rightarrow$ `analysis` $\rightarrow$ `report`) [src/fastmdxplora/cli/main.py:6-6](), [docs/cli.md:22-23]() |
| `setup` | Execute system preparation (PDB fixing, protonation, solvation, ionization) and terminate [src/fastmdxplora/cli/main.py:7-7](), [docs/cli.md:24-24]() |
| `simulate` | Run molecular dynamics equilibration and production phases on a prepared system [src/fastmdxplora/cli/main.py:8-8](), [docs/cli.md:25-25]() |
| `analyze` | Perform trajectory analyses (RMSD, RMSF, hydrogen bonds, etc.) [src/fastmdxplora/cli/main.py:9-9](), [docs/cli.md:26-26]() |
| `report` | Generate document/slide summaries and metrics reports [src/fastmdxplora/cli/main.py:10-10](), [docs/cli.md:27-27]() |
| `gui` | Launch the localhost web dashboard server [docs/cli.md:29-29]() |
| `info` | Print local environment, hardware, and dependency diagnostic info [src/fastmdxplora/cli/main.py:11-11](), [docs/cli.md:36-36]() |
| `remote` | Inspect and manage remote execution nodes over SSH [src/fastmdxplora/cli/main.py:12-13](), [docs/cli.md:37-37]() |
| `agent` | Invoke the AI Agent proposal and generation loop [docs/cli.md:28-28]() |
| `mcp` | Serve FastMDXplora tools via the Model Context Protocol [docs/cli.md:30-30]() |
| `config` | Write a heavily-commented default configuration template [docs/cli.md:31-31]() |
| `select` | Evaluate and print atom selections prior to execution [docs/cli.md:32-32]() |
| `diff` | Compute differences between two configuration files or studies [docs/cli.md:33-33]() |
| `scene` | Export a molecular view as a MolViewSpec (`.mvsx`) scene file [docs/cli.md:34-34]() |
| `movie` | Render trajectory frames into movie files via local `ffmpeg` [docs/cli.md:35-35]() |
| `resume` | Continue an interrupted or prematurely stopped study [docs/cli.md:38-38]() |

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/cli/main.py:1-24` [src/fastmdxplora/cli/main.py:1-24](), `docs/cli.md:18-39` [docs/cli.md:18-39]()

---

## 3. Schema-Derived Flags and Naming Conventions

The CLI constructs options programmatically to mirror phase configuration schemas. Flag names follow a strict prefix convention based on whether they are invoked globally via `explore` or locally via phase-specific subcommands [docs/cli.md:51-64]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph NaturalLanguageSpace ["CLI Flag Pattern"]
        A["--setup-ph 7.0"]
        B["--ph 7.0"]
    end

    subgraph CodeEntitySpace ["Schema Mapping & Config Resolution"]
        A -->|"--explore subcommand prefix"| C["_SETUP_OPTIONS mapping"]
        B -->|"--setup subcommand context"| C
        C -->|coerces to kwarg| D["run_setup(ph=7.0)"]
    end

    style NaturalLanguageSpace fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style CodeEntitySpace fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
```
*Diagram 2: Mapping natural language CLI options to internal phase keyword arguments.*

When using `explore`, settings are prefixed by their target phase name (`--setup-`, `--simulate-`, `--analyze-`, `--report-`, `--execution-`) [docs/cli.md:61-64](). When running a single-phase subcommand directly, the prefix is omitted [docs/cli.md:57-58]().

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/cli/main.py:50-105` [src/fastmdxplora/cli/main.py:50-105](), `docs/cli.md:51-78` [docs/cli.md:51-78]()

---

## 4. Configuration, Defaults Files, and Execution Modifiers

Execution behavior can be modified through input declarations, override rules, and defaults files (`fastmdx-defaults.yml`) [docs/cli.md:105-113]().

- **Input Declaration**: `-s` / `--system` accepts local PDB/CIF paths or 4-character PDB identifiers, automatically resolving structure sources [docs/cli.md:107-107]().
- **Configuration Override**: `-c` / `--config` loads a base YAML configuration file, which is subsequently overridden by explicit CLI flags [docs/cli.md:108-108]().
- **Defaults Suppression**: `--no-defaults` disables the automatic discovery and application of nearest `fastmdx-defaults.yml` profile files [docs/cli.md:112-112]().
- **Execution Dry-Runs**: `--dry-run` validates all parameters, prints the resolved execution plan, and terminates without creating output artifacts [docs/cli.md:135-135]().

Sources: `docs/cli.md:92-150` [docs/cli.md:92-150]()

---

# Page: Orchestrator and Batch Campaigns

# Orchestrator and Batch Campaigns

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

## Purpose and Scope
This page details the orchestration and batch campaign architecture of FastMDXplora. It covers the phase-based execution engine (`FastMDXplora`), data structures (`RunResult` and `PhaseResult`), parameter sweeps (`BatchExplorer`), process-level parallelization with round-robin GPU device pinning, cross-run comparison/aggregation, and local workspace resource/GPU sharing.

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/orchestrator.py:1-174()`, `src/fastmdxplora/batch/explorer.py:1-38()`

---

## 1. Orchestrator Phases and Data Structures

FastMDXplora follows a built-in phase-based orchestration pattern rather than a generic Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) workflow engine. The workflow consists of four canonical phases executed in a strict sequence: setup, simulation, analysis, and report (`src/fastmdxplora/orchestrator.py:56-58()`).

Each phase invocation yields a `PhaseResult` dataclass instance (`src/fastmdxplora/orchestrator.py:94-105()`), capturing:
- `name`: The phase identifier (`setup`, `simulation`, `analysis`, `report`).
- `status`: Execution outcome (`ok`, `skipped`, `error`).
- `output_dir`: Path to phase-specific outputs.
- `started_at` / `finished_at`: Timestamp string telemetry.
- `artifacts`: List of generated files relative to the phase directory.
- `refusal`: Structured refusal dictionary (`src/fastmdxplora/orchestrator.py:105-117()`).
- `produced_by`: Environment, version, and host provenance records (`src/fastmdxplora/orchestrator.py:118-131()`).

A complete study or individual sweep run is encapsulated by `RunResult` (`src/fastmdxplora/orchestrator.py:159-174()`), which aggregates the `run_id`, target system, global status, output directory, sweep parameters, and list of `phases`.

Diagram: Orchestrator Execution Flow and Data Structures
```mermaid
graph TD
    A["UserIntent / CLI"] -->|Config / Args| B["FastMDXplora (orchestrator.py)"]
    B -->|Iterate PHASES| C["Setup Phase"]
    C -->|PhaseResult| D["Simulation Phase"]
    D -->|PhaseResult| E["Analysis Phase"]
    E -->|PhaseResult| F["Report Phase"]
    F -->|Consolidate| G["RunResult (orchestrator.py)"]
    G -->|Write| H["manifest.json"]

    subcode["Code Entity Mapping"]
    PHASES["PHASES tuple (orchestrator.py:58)"]
    PhaseResultClass["PhaseResult (orchestrator.py:94)"]
    RunResultClass["RunResult (orchestrator.py:159)"]
    end
```
Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/orchestrator.py:1-174()`

---

## 2. Batch Campaigns and Sweep Expansion

FastMDXplora unifies single-run execution and parameter sweeps into a single code path via `BatchExplorer` (`src/fastmdxplora/batch/explorer.py:1-15()`). A single-system configuration is treated simply as a batch size of one (`src/fastmdxplora/batch/explorer.py:3-6()`).

### Output Layout Adaptation
The output directory layout adapts based on the run count (`src/fastmdxplora/batch/explorer.py:8-15()`):
- **Single run**: Flat layout written directly to the target output directory (`output/setup/`, `output/simulation/`, etc.), containing the root `manifest.json` and `resolved_config.yml`. No `runs/` wrapper folder is created.
- **Multiple runs / Sweeps**: Each run is placed in `output/runs/<id>/` as an isolated study directory, accompanied by a top-level `batch_manifest.json` indexing all member runs.

### Sweep Expansion
Parameter sweeps and multiple systems are normalized and expanded via `expand_runs` and `normalize_sweep` (`src/fastmdxplora/batch/explorer.py:55-60()`), generating a list of immutable `RunSpec` objects that resolve configuration inheritance (`base < per-system < sweep`).

Diagram: Batch Explorer Execution Path
```mermaid
graph TD
    I["Batch Configuration file"] --> J["expand_runs (sweep.py)"]
    J --> K["List of RunSpec"]
    K --> L{"Run Count == 1?"}
    L -->|Yes| M["Flat Directory Output (setup/, simulation/)"]
    L -->|No| N["Runs Subdirectory (runs/<id>/) + batch_manifest.json"]
    M --> O["BatchExplorer (explorer.py)"]
    N --> O

    subcode2["Code Entity Mapping"]
    ExplorerClass["BatchExplorer (explorer.py)"]
    SweepExpander["expand_runs (sweep.py)"]
    end
```
Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/batch/explorer.py:1-60()`, `src/fastmdxplora/batch/sweep.py:1-60()`

---

## 3. Parallel Execution and Device Pinning

Execution modes are governed by the `execution:` configuration block (`src/fastmdxplora/batch/explorer.py:17-38()`):
- `sequential`: Runs studies one after another within the primary process.
- `parallel`: Dispatches runs across a process pool of size `workers` using `ProcessPoolExecutor` (`src/fastmdxplora/batch/explorer.py:46-51()`). Process-based parallelism is mandatory because OpenMM contexts and the Python GIL do not share safely across threads (`src/fastmdxplora/batch/explorer.py:35-37()`).

### GPU Device Pinning
When `devices: [0, 1, ...]` is specified alongside parallel execution, workers are pinned to distinct GPU devices in a round-robin fashion (one run per GPU) (`src/fastmdxplora/batch/explorer.py:20-23()`). Device assignment injects `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` into the worker subprocess environment. 

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/batch/explorer.py:17-52()`

---

## 4. Comparison, Aggregation and Workspace GPU Sharing

### Comparison and Aggregation
Campaign outcomes can be analyzed collectively using comparison and aggregation modules (`src/fastmdxplora/batch/compare.py`, `src/fastmdxplora/batch/aggregate.py`). These utilities scan batch run directories, extract time-series metrics (e.g., RMSD, energy, hydrogen bonds), compute statistical summaries, and align trajectories across distinct sweep parameters.

### Local GPU Sharing and Workspace Concurrency
When running multiple studies concurrently on a single local workstation, FastMDXplora prevents race conditions and VRAM oversubscription through workspace runtime controls (`src/fastmdxplora/runs_here.py`, `src/fastmdxplora/gpu_here.py`):
- **Starting Locks**: Workspace initialization and study spawning hold an OS-level file lock (`STARTING_FILE`, `.fastmdxplora-starting`) to serialize concurrent start requests (`src/fastmdxplora/runs_here.py:46-95()`).
- **Active Run Registry**: Started studies record their process metadata, directory, and allocated GPU UUID in `RUNS_FILE` (`.fastmdxplora-runs.json`) (`src/fastmdxplora/runs_here.py:52-54()`).
- **VRAM Accounting**: The `gpu_room` subsystem queries local GPU memory usage (via `nvidia-smi` or cached empirical learning profiles) to verify whether an incoming study fits within available VRAM before dispatching (`src/fastmdxplora/remote/gpu_room.py`).

Diagram: Workspace and GPU Concurrency Management
```mermaid
graph TD
    P["Incoming Study Start Request"] --> Q["starting_in (runs_here.py)"]
    Q -->|Acquire OS File Lock| R[".fastmdxplora-starting"]
    R --> S["may_start Check (gpu_here.py)"]
    S --> T{"VRAM Available?"}
    T -->|No| U["Refuse with No Room Error"]
    T -->|Yes| V["Allocate GPU / CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES"]
    V --> W["Record Run in .fastmdxplora-runs.json"]
    W --> X["Spawn Subprocess Execution"]

    subcode3["Code Entity Mappings"]
    WorkspaceLock["starting_in (runs_here.py:72)"]
    GpuRoomCheck["may_start (runs_here.py)"]
    end
```
Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/runs_here.py:1-173()`, `src/fastmdxplora/gpu_here.py:1-50()`, `src/fastmdxplora/remote/gpu_room.py:1-50()`

---

# Scientific Pipeline

## Purpose and Scope

The FastMDXplora scientific pipeline transforms raw molecular structures into rigorous thermodynamic and dynamic insights through four sequential phases: setup, simulation, analysis, and report generation. Artifacts flow deterministically between these phases using structured file bundles (`system.xml`, `state.xml`, trajectories, and JSON manifests) stored within a study workspace. 

This page provides a high-level architectural overview of how the pipeline stages interact. For detailed technical specifications, deep-dive configuration options, and implementation specifics, refer to the child pages linked throughout.

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/setup/pipeline.py:1-45` [src/fastmdxplora/setup/pipeline.py:1-45](), `src/fastmdxplora/simulation/pipeline.py:1-44` [src/fastmdxplora/simulation/pipeline.py:1-44]()

---

## Pipeline Artifact Flow

The diagram below maps the natural language space of user study requests and configuration blocks to the underlying code entities that execute each phase of the scientific pipeline.

Title: Pipeline Artifact Flow and Code Entities

```mermaid
graph TD
    UserRequest[""UserStructureOrPDB""] --> SetupPhase[""run (setup/pipeline.py)""]
    SetupPhase --> PreparedArtifacts[""system.xml, state.xml, topology.pdb (setup/prepare.py)""]
    PreparedArtifacts --> SimPhase[""run (simulation/pipeline.py)""]
    SimPhase --> Runner[""run_simulation (simulation/runner.py)""]
    Runner --> Trajectory[""TrajectoryFramesAndLogs""]
    Trajectory --> AnalysisPhase[""AnalysisOrchestrator""]
    AnalysisPhase --> ReportPhase[""ReportGeneratorAndStatistics""]
    
    subgraph NaturalLanguageSpace
        UserRequest
    end

    subgraph CodeEntitySpace
        SetupPhase
        PreparedArtifacts
        SimPhase
        Runner
        Trajectory
        AnalysisPhase
        ReportPhase
    end
```

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/setup/pipeline.py:1-25` [src/fastmdxplora/setup/pipeline.py:1-25](), `src/fastmdxplora/simulation/pipeline.py:1-12` [src/fastmdxplora/simulation/pipeline.py:1-12](), `src/fastmdxplora/simulation/runner.py:1-14` [src/fastmdxplora/simulation/runner.py:1-14]()

---

## 3.1 Setup Phase: System Preparation

The setup phase bridges raw structural inputs (PDB files, RCSB accession codes, or sequences) to a parameterised, solvated, and neutralised OpenMM system. It resolves force fields, handles missing residues or heavy atoms via PDBFixer, assigns protonation states at a target pH, and packs periodic water boxes with specified ionic strengths.

For detailed information on heterogen management, CCD lookups, membrane building, and size estimation checks, see [Setup Phase: System Preparation](#3.1).

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/setup/pipeline.py:1-25` [src/fastmdxplora/setup/pipeline.py:1-25](), `src/fastmdxplora/setup/prepare.py:1-39` [src/fastmdxplora/setup/prepare.py:1-39]()

---

## 3.2 Simulation Phase

The simulation phase consumes the serialized `system.xml`, `state.xml`, and `topology.pdb` artifacts produced during setup. It executes an OpenMM-backed runner across multiple compute platforms (CUDA, OpenCL, CPU) while recording telemetry, enforcing stage planning, and managing execution checkpoints.

For deep technical details on integrators, barostats, and enhanced sampling, see [Simulation Phase](#3.2).

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/simulation/pipeline.py:1-44` [src/fastmdxplora/simulation/pipeline.py:1-44](), `src/fastmdxplora/simulation/runner.py:1-18` [src/fastmdxplora/simulation/runner.py:1-18]()

### 3.2.1 MD Runner, Platforms and Checkpoints

The core runner executes a standard four-stage MD pipeline: energy minimization, NVT equilibration, NPT equilibration, and production run execution. It handles variable-step integrators, thermal bath coupling via Langevin thermostats, barostat frequency adjustments, and checkpoint seal verifications.

For details on stage parameters, resume logic, and stop graces, see [MD Runner, Platforms and Checkpoints](#3.2.1).

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/simulation/runner.py:1-14` [src/fastmdxplora/simulation/runner.py:1-14](), `src/fastmdxplora/simulation/runner.py:120-159` [src/fastmdxplora/simulation/runner.py:120-159]()

### 3.2.2 Enhanced Sampling and Free Energy

When standard production dynamics are insufficient to cross high free-energy barriers, FastMDXplora integrates advanced sampling methodologies. These include umbrella sampling with WHAM post-processing, well-tempered metadynamics, steered molecular dynamics, and PLUMED plugin orchestration.

For specific configuration guides and free energy profile calculations, see [Enhanced Sampling and Free Energy](#3.2.2).

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/simulation/pipeline.py:139-158` [src/fastmdxplora/simulation/pipeline.py:139-158]()

---

## 3.3 Analysis Phase

The analysis phase processes trajectory frames generated during production MD to extract structural, dynamic, thermodynamic, and ligand-interaction metrics. The framework uses a registered list of analyses ranging from foundational metrics like RMSD and radius of gyration to complex spatial distribution functions.

For a comprehensive catalog of available analysis routines and trajectory loading conventions, see [Analysis Phase](#3.3).

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/config/schema.py:41-76` [src/fastmdxplora/config/schema.py:41-76]()

### 3.3.1 Structural and Dynamic Analyses

Structural evaluations track macromolecular stability, backbone fluctuations, compactness, solvent-accessible surface area, and secondary structure persistence across time. 

For implementation details on RMSD, RMSF, Rg, SASA, and hydrogen bonding calculations, see [Structural and Dynamic Analyses](#3.3.1).

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/config/schema.py:45-50` [src/fastmdxplora/config/schema.py:45-50]()

### 3.3.2 Ligand, Interaction and Solvent Analyses

Protein-ligand systems require specialized scrutiny. This subsection covers ligand RMSD/RMSF tracking, contact map generation, hydrogen bond occupancy, and hydration shell (water site) characterization.

For detailed protocols on binding site solvent dynamics and interaction profiling, see [Ligand, Interaction and Solvent Analyses](#3.3.2).

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/config/schema.py:46-48` [src/fastmdxplora/config/schema.py:46-48]()

### 3.3.3 Membrane, Thermodynamic and Reweighted Analyses

For membrane-embedded systems and biased simulations, specialized metrics evaluate bilayer thickness, area per lipid, lipid acyl-chain order parameters, system thermodynamics, and WHAM/metadynamics reweighted averages.

For complete coverage of membrane and reweighted observable pipelines, see [Membrane, Thermodynamic and Reweighted Analyses](#3.3.3).

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/config/schema.py:55-64` [src/fastmdxplora/config/schema.py:55-64](), `src/fastmdxplora/config/schema.py:72-75` [src/fastmdxplora/config/schema.py:72-75]()

---

## 3.4 Report Phase and Statistics

The report phase synthesizes artifact records, trajectory summaries, and statistical evaluations into publication-ready documents, presentation slides, or PDF summaries. It handles automated methods prose generation, convergence assessments, and statistical inefficiency calculations to ensure reproducibility and transparency before study deposition.

For details on report compilation, statistical withholding rules, and export bundles, see [Report Phase and Statistics](#3.4).

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/config/schema.py:4-25` [src/fastmdxplora/config/schema.py:4-25]()

---

The setup phase transforms raw structural inputs (PDB files, RCSB PDB IDs, or sequences) into a fully-parameterized, solvated, and ionized molecular system ready for simulation. Declared under the setup schema registry [src/fastmdxplora/config/schema.py:37-37](), this phase executes a robust chemistry pipeline that enforces structural plausibility, governs heterogen retention, determines ligand protonation states *in complex* via PROPKA, loads small molecules via OpenFF, assigns force fields, handles membrane bilayers, and serializes OpenMM artifacts (`system.xml`, `state.xml`, and `topology.pdb`).

```mermaid
graph TD
    Input["User Input (PDB/CIF/ID)"] --> Classify["_classify_input()"]
    Classify -->|PDB ID| Fetch["_retrieve() / RCSB"]
    Classify -->|File Path| Fix["fix_pdb_with_pdbfixer()"]
    Fetch --> Fix
    Fix --> Het["Heterogen & Capping Protection"]
    Het --> Prot["Protonation State Settlement (PROPKA)"]
    Prot --> Prep["prepare_system()"]
    Prep --> Solv["Modeller addSolvent & Ionize"]
    Solv --> Plausible["_refuse_an_implausible_structure()"]
    Plausible --> Serialize["Serialize System.xml & State.xml"]
```
*Sources: [src/fastmdxplora/setup/pipeline.py:7-13](), [src/fastmdxplora/setup/prepare.py:73-88](), [src/fastmdxplora/setup/pdbfix.py:17-25]()*

---

## Input Resolution, Fetching and PDB Repair

The entry point for system preparation is managed by `src/fastmdxplora/setup/pipeline.py` [src/fastmdxplora/setup/pipeline.py:1-25](), which classifies the system input into `pdb_file`, `pdb_id`, or `sequence` using `_classify_input` [src/fastmdxplora/setup/pipeline.py:74-81](). If a 4-character alphanumeric PDB ID is supplied, structures are fetched from the RCSB data bank using `_retrieve` [src/fastmdxplora/setup/pipeline.py:154-156](), complete with transient error recovery and retry delays (`_FETCH_WAITS_S`) [src/fastmdxplora/setup/pipeline.py:118-122]() for reset or busy connections handled by `_passes` [src/fastmdxplora/setup/pipeline.py:126-132]().

Once raw structural coordinates are acquired, `src/fastmdxplora/setup/pdbfix.py` executes structural repair via PDBFixer. This includes:
1. Removing unwanted heterogens while sparing recognized ligands and capping groups (`_protect_capping_groups`) [src/fastmdxplora/setup/pdbfix.py:69-98]().
2. Detecting and filling missing residues and heavy atoms [src/fastmdxplora/setup/pdbfix.py:21-23]().
3. Adding missing hydrogens at the user-specified pH using `addMissingHydrogens` [src/fastmdxplora/setup/pdbfix.py:24-24]().

Prior to solvation, `src/fastmdxplora/setup/prepare.py` runs `_refuse_an_implausible_structure` [src/fastmdxplora/setup/prepare.py:73-88](). This prevents wasted computation on broken or expanded coordinates by estimating maximum expected spatial extent based on residue counts:

$$\text{plausible} = 4.0 \times N_{\text{residues}}^{1/3}$$

If the structural bounding box extent exceeds this threshold—typically caused by terminal loops walking off into infinity without anchor points—preparation halts with `StudyError` (`setup.structure.implausible_extent`) [src/fastmdxplora/setup/prepare.py:110-123]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    Start["_classify_input()"] --> CheckFile{".pdb or .cif?"}
    CheckFile -->|Yes| ReadFile["Verify Local Path"]
    CheckFile -->|No| CheckID{"4-char Alphanumeric?"}
    CheckID -->|Yes| FetchRCSB["_retrieve() from RCSB"]
    CheckID -->|No| SeqErr["Raise setup.input.unrecognised"]
    ReadFile --> PDBFix["pdbfix.py: PDBFixer Repair"]
    FetchRCSB --> PDBFix
    PDBFix --> Extent["_refuse_an_implausible_structure()"]
    Extent -->|Valid| Solvation["Proceed to Solvation"]
    Extent -->|Invalid| Refuse["Raise StudyError (Implausible Extent)"]
```
*Sources: [src/fastmdxplora/setup/pipeline.py:74-115](), [src/fastmdxplora/setup/pdbfix.py:17-25](), [src/fastmdxplora/setup/prepare.py:73-123病毒]*

---

## Heterogen Classification and Filtering

Crystal structures frequently contain crystallization buffers, salts, polyols, cryoprotectants, and extraneous molecules alongside biological polymers. `src/fastmdxplora/setup/heterogens.py` classifies non-standard residues into three strict outcomes under the `Action` enumeration: `SIMULATE`, `DISCARD`, or `STOP` [src/fastmdxplora/setup/heterogens.py:36-42]().

To avoid silent substitution of apo trajectories for holo runs or accidental simulation of cryoprotectants, heterogens are filtered according to curated sets:
- **Solvent & Ions**: Standard water names (`WATER_NAMES`) and monatomic ions (`ION_NAMES`) are stripped or treated systematically [src/fastmdxplora/setup/heterogens.py:44-53]().
- **Crystallization Additives**: Additives like glycerol (`GOL`), PEG, and buffer molecules (`EPE`, `MES`, `TRS`) in `CRYSTALLIZATION_ADDITIVES` are safely discarded [src/fastmdxplora/setup/heterogens.py:60-77]() with explicit reporting (`_heterogen_residue_counts`) [src/fastmdxplora/setup/pdbfix.py:157-166]() so that no ligand or buffer deletion occurs silently [tests/test_setup_layer.py:39-45]().
- **Ambiguous Sugars & Cofactors**: Glycosylation residues and unparameterizable cofactors (`UNPARAMETERIZABLE` such as `HEM`, `FAD`, iron-sulfur clusters) trigger explicit stops if they lack force-field template support [src/fastmdxplora/setup/heterogens.py:79-114]().

*Sources: [src/fastmdxplora/setup/heterogens.py:1-125](), [src/fastmdxplora/setup/pdbfix.py:157-166]()*

---

## Protonation State Determination

Predicting ligand protonation states using isolated in-water rule tables frequently misrepresents buried or pocket-bound chemical states where pKa shifts of 2–3 units occur [src/fastmdxplora/setup/protonation.py:1-9](). `src/fastmdxplora/setup/protonation.py` delegates this task to PROPKA, evaluating ionizable groups directly within the 3D atomic environment of the protein-ligand complex [src/fastmdxplora/setup/protonation.py:10-18]().

The settlement logic (`decide`) inspects calculated `GroupPka` records against the simulation `pH`:
1. **Determined States**: If computed pKas lie comfortably outside the buffer band defined by `POISED_MARGIN` (default `1.0` pH unit) [src/fastmdxplora/setup/protonation.py:43-58](), the protonation state (`ProtonationState`) is assigned with explicit provenance reasons [src/fastmdxplora/setup/protonation.py:101-107]().
2. **Poised Groups**: If a group's pKa falls within $\pm 1.0$ of the simulation pH, both protonated and deprotonated forms are appreciably populated; preparation halts and raises a `ProtonationError` [src/fastmdxplora/setup/protonation.py:53-58]().
3. **Undetermined Inputs**: If an ionizable ligand yields no PROPKA output, preparation refuses to fall back to generic rule tables, guaranteeing chemical safety [tests/test_protonation.py:62-70]().

*Sources: [src/fastmdxplora/setup/protonation.py:1-76](), [tests/test_protonation.py:52-77]()*

---

## Ligand Parameterization and CCD

Small-molecule ligands and cofactors are loaded and validated via `src/fastmdxplora/setup/ligand.py` [src/fastmdxplora/setup/ligand.py:1-18](). SDF and MOL2 are the sole supported input formats because they supply complete bond-order and explicit charge data required by the OpenFF toolkit (`SystemGenerator`) [src/fastmdxplora/setup/ligand.py:35-59](). PDB `HETATM` extractions are intentionally rejected due to missing bond topology [src/fastmdxplora/setup/ligand.py:55-58]().

Key functions in the ligand module include:
- `detect_ligand_format()`: Validates file suffixes against `SUPPORTED_LIGAND_FORMATS` (`sdf`, `mol2`) [src/fastmdxplora/setup/ligand.py:43-59]().
- `am1bcc_provider()`: Detects available charging backends (`AmberTools` via `sqm` or `OpenEye`) to assign AM1-BCC charges for OpenFF/GAFF force fields [src/fastmdxplora/setup/ligand.py:85-120]().
- `pose_by_policy()`: Implements coordinate source selection policies (`auto`, `structure`, `file`), ensuring that control runs (such as unbound docking poses) are chosen explicitly rather than introduced by accident [src/fastmdxplora/setup/ligand.py:122-160]().

*Sources: [src/fastmdxplora/setup/ligand.py:1-160]()*

---

## Force Field Selection and System Preparation

System preparation culminates in `src/fastmdxplora/setup/prepare.py` [src/fastmdxplora/setup/prepare.py:1-39](), where OpenMM Modeller builds periodic boundary boxes, adds water, and neutralizes charges with counter-ions.

- **Default Force Field**: `forcefield: auto` resolves to `amber-openff` (`amber14-all.xml` + `amber14/tip3p.xml` combined with OpenFF small-molecule parameterization) [src/fastmdxplora/setup/prepare.py:21-31](). 
- **Solvation and Ionization**: Modeller places the solute inside a configurable box shape (`cube`, `dodecahedron`, `octahedron`) with padding (`DEFAULT_PADDING_NM = 1.0` nm) [src/fastmdxplora/setup/prepare.py:66-66] and sets ionic strength (`DEFAULT_IONIC_STRENGTH_M = 0.15` M) [src/fastmdxplora/setup/prepare.py:67-67]().
- **Serialization**: The pipeline outputs four canonical artifacts consumed by simulation and analysis phases:
  - `solvated.pdb` (and its alias `topology.pdb`) [src/fastmdxplora/setup/prepare.py:34-36]()
  - `system.xml` (serialized OpenMM `System`) [src/fastmdxplora/setup/prepare.py:37-37]()
  - `state.xml` (serialized initial OpenMM `State`) [src/fastmdxplora/setup/prepare.py:38-38]()

*Sources: [src/fastmdxplora/setup/prepare.py:1-39](), [src/fastmdxplora/setup/prepare.py:66-67]*

---

## Membrane Insertion and Size Estimation

Embedding membrane proteins requires specialized lipid parameterization and anisotropic barostat configuration. `src/fastmdxplora/setup/membrane.py` and `src/fastmdxplora/setup/membrane_fit.py` detect lipid environments from topologies (`is_membrane_system`, `is_bilayer`) [tests/test_membrane.py:93-119]() and automatically inject missing lipid XML parameters into force-field file lists (e.g., adding `charmm36.xml` when lipid tags are present) [tests/test_membrane.py:33-55](). 

Simultaneously, `src/fastmdxplora/setup/estimate.py` estimates system dimensions, memory footprints, and expected wall-clock durations based on atom and water counts prior to heavy resource allocation.

*Sources: [src/fastmdxplora/setup/membrane.py](), [src/fastmdxplora/setup/estimate.py](), [tests/test_membrane.py:1-160]()*

---

# Page: Simulation Phase

# Simulation Phase

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/fastmdxplora/config/schema.py](src/fastmdxplora/config/schema.py)
- [src/fastmdxplora/simulation/pipeline.py](src/fastmdxplora/simulation/pipeline.py)
- [src/fastmdxplora/simulation/runner.py](src/fastmdxplora/simulation/runner.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

The Simulation Phase is responsible for executing molecular dynamics (MD) simulations using the OpenMM backend [src/fastmdxplora/simulation/runner.py:1-18](). It consumes serialized preparation artifacts (`system.xml`, `state.xml`, and `topology.pdb`) produced during the setup phase and executes a standardized four-stage integration pipeline: energy minimization, NVT equilibration, NPT equilibration, and production MD [src/fastmdxplora/simulation/pipeline.py:1-12](). 

This page provides a high-level overview of the simulation subsystem, its stage planning, configuration resolution, and ties to enhanced-sampling methodologies. For deep technical details on execution flags, barostats, checkpointing, and advanced free-energy methods, refer to the child pages:
- [MD Runner, Platforms and Checkpoints](#3.2.1)
- [Enhanced Sampling and Free Energy](#3.2.2)

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/simulation/runner.py:1-18`, `src/fastmdxplora/simulation/pipeline.py:1-44`

---

## Simulation Pipeline Architecture

The orchestration-facing pipeline module (`fastmdxplora.simulation.pipeline`) coordinates asset verification before invoking the core OpenMM runner (`fastmdxplora.simulation.runner`) [src/fastmdxplora/simulation/pipeline.py:1-12](). It checks for prepared system geometries across standard layout paths via `where_a_prepared_system_sits()` [src/fastmdxplora/simulation/pipeline.py:112-136]() and handles graceful degradation if OpenMM or preparation files are absent [src/fastmdxplora/simulation/pipeline.py:37-44]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["setup_outputs_present"] -->|Validates XML/PDB| B["run_simulation"]
    B --> C[MinimizationStage]
    C --> D[NVTEqStage]
    D --> E[NPTEqStage]
    E --> F[ProductionStage]
    F --> G["SimulationResult"]

    style A fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style B fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style C fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style D fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style E fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style F fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style G fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
```
*Figure 1: High-level pipeline stage transitions managed by the simulation subsystem.*

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/simulation/pipeline.py:1-105`, `src/fastmdxplora/simulation/runner.py:1-150`

---

## Configuration and Parameter Resolution

Simulation options are declared centrally within the configuration schema registry (`fastmdxplora.config.schema`) [src/fastmdxplora/config/schema.py:1-25](). The pipeline reads these defaults via `SIMULATION.defaults()` and merges user overrides through `_resolve_params()` [src/fastmdxplora/simulation/pipeline.py:64-82](). 

Standard default parameters include:
- **Minimization**: Conducted until convergence with a default tolerance of `10.0` kJ/mol/nm [src/fastmdxplora/runner.py:116]() (`DEFAULT_MINIMIZE_TOLERANCE_KJMOL_PER_NM`).
- **NVT Equilibration**: Default duration of `500` ps (250,000 steps at a 2 fs timestep) using a Langevin thermostat.
- **NPT Equilibration**: Default duration of `1` ns (500,000 steps at 2 fs) with a Monte Carlo barostat.
- **Production MD**: Default duration of `2` ns (1,000,000 steps at 2 fs), producing trajectory frames consumed by the analysis phase [src/fastmdxplora/simulation/pipeline.py:15-35]().

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/config/schema.py:1-25`, `src/fastmdxplora/simulation/pipeline.py:64-82`, `src/fastmdxplora/simulation/runner.py:116-123`

---

This leaf page details the implementation of FastMDXplora's OpenMM-backed molecular dynamics runner, covering the execution of the four-stage simulation pipeline (`src/fastmdxplora/simulation/runner.py:1-18]`), platform configuration, integrators, barostats, restraint schedules, telemetry emission, checkpoint seals, and the resumption/extension engine (`src/fastmdxplora/simulation/resume.py:1-41]`).

---

## 1. The Four-Stage Simulation Pipeline

The simulation phase takes the serialized OpenMM `System`, `State`, and `Topology` files generated during setup and executes a standardized four-stage pipeline:
1. **Minimization**: Local energy minimization using a specified force-tolerance (`src/fastmdxplora/simulation/runner.py:6-6`).
2. **NVT Equilibration**: Constant volume equilibration using a Langevin thermostat (`src/fastmdxplora/simulation/runner.py:7-7`).
3. **NPT Equilibration**: Constant pressure equilibration introducing a Monte Carlo barostat (`src/fastmdxplora/simulation/runner.py:8-8`).
4. **Production**: Long-duration sampling generating trajectory frames consumed by downstream analysis phases (`src/fastmdxplora/simulation/runner.py:9-9`).

The orchestrator interfaces via `src/fastmdxplora/simulation/pipeline.py` which verifies setup artifacts (`src/fastmdxplora/simulation/pipeline.py:85-93]`) and delegates execution to `fastmdxplora.simulation.runner.run_simulation` (`src/fastmdxplora/simulation/pipeline.py:8-8`). The output metadata and paths are encapsulated within the immutable `SimulationResult` data class (`src/fastmdxplora/simulation/runner.py:128-160]`).

```mermaid
graph TD
    sub5[""src/fastmdxplora/simulation/pipeline.py""] -->|"calls run"| sub6[""src/fastmdxplora/simulation/runner.py""]
    sub6 -->|"Stage 1"| A[""Minimization""]
    A -->|"Stage 2"| B[""NVT_Equilibration""]
    B -->|"Stage 3"| C[""NPT_Equilibration""]
    C -->|"Stage 4"| D[""Production_MD""]
    D -->|"Returns"| E[""SimulationResult""]

    classDef default fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px;
```
*Figure 1: Pipeline stage execution flow mapping orchestrator entry points to OpenMM runner routines.*

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/simulation/runner.py:1-18]`, `src/fastmdxplora/simulation/runner.py:128-160]`, `src/fastmdxplora/simulation/pipeline.py:1-44]`

---

## 2. Integrators, Platforms and Barostats

OpenMM operations rely on hardware backends resolved dynamically via CLI or configuration flags (`docs/production.md:13-16]`). 

### Platforms and Precision
- Supported precision-aware GPU platforms are defined in `PRECISION_PLATFORMS` (`src/fastmdxplora/simulation/runner.py:49-52]`): `CUDA`, `OpenCL`, and `HIP`.
- OpenMM is imported lazily to ensure project-level imports do not fail in environments lacking simulation dependencies (`src/fastmdxplora/simulation/runner.py:15-18]`, `src/fastmdxplora/simulation/runner.py:164-171]`).

### Integrators
The runner supports multiple integration schemes (`SUPPORTED_INTEGRATORS`), defaulting to `langevin_middle` for enhanced configurational sampling stability compared to legacy Langevin algorithms (`src/fastmdxplora/simulation/runner.py:63-81]`):
- Fixed-step integrators (`langevin`, `langevin_middle`, `brownian`, `verlet`).
- Variable-step integrators (`variable_langevin`, `variable_verlet`) grouped under `VARIABLE_STEP_INTEGRATORS` (`src/fastmdxplora/simulation/runner.py:73-74]`). Variable-step runs determine elapsed times dynamically; helper functions such as `chose_its_own_step()` inspect simulation parameter records to handle trajectory timing metrics (`src/fastmdxplora/simulation/runner.py:84-112]`).

### Barostats and Ensembles
Constant-pressure stages (NPT) configure Monte Carlo barostats (`DEFAULT_BAROSTAT_FREQUENCY`, `src/fastmdxplora/simulation/runner.py:61-62]`), tracking metrics such as `pressure_bar_used` and `barostat` (isotropic or membrane coupling) inside `SimulationResult` (`src/fastmdxplora/simulation/runner.py:143-148]`).

```mermaid
graph TD
    sub7[""ResolvedConfig/CLI""] -->|"selects platform"| P[""PRECISION_PLATFORMS: CUDA/OpenCL/HIP""]
    sub7 -->|"selects integrator"| I[""SUPPORTED_INTEGRATORS: langevin_middle""]
    I -->|"variable step check"| V[""VARIABLE_STEP_INTEGRATORS""]
    sub7 -->|"selects ensemble"| E[""NPT / NVT Resolution""]
    E -->|"barostat config"| B[""MonteCarloBarostat (isotropic/membrane)""]

    classDef default fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px;
```
*Figure 2: Configuration routing for simulation hardware platforms, numerical integrators, and thermodynamic ensembles.*

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/simulation/runner.py:49-112]`, `src/fastmdxplora/simulation/runner.py:128-160]`, `docs/production.md:13-16]`

---

## 3. Restraints and Release Schedules

Equilibration protocols incorporate position or geometry restraints to stabilize solute conformations while solvent molecules relax (`tests/test_restraints.py:1-9]`). 

### Restraint Parsing
The parser validates restraint configurations via `parse_restraints()` (`tests/test_restraints.py:62-117]`):
- Short-form inputs parse positional selections using default force constants (`DEFAULT_POSITION_FORCE`, `tests/test_restraints.py:68-71]`).
- Complex restraint lists (`position`, `distance`, `torsion`) enforce explicit force constant declarations where conventional defaults do not apply (`tests/test_restraints.py:79-98]`).
- Units are validated according to physical dimensions (`kJ/mol/nm^2` for positions/distances versus `kJ/mol/rad^2` for torsions) (`tests/test_restraints.py:105-117]`).

### Release Schedules
`ReleaseSchedule` governs the gradual attenuation of restraint forces during equilibration stages to prevent energetic shocks or structural lurches (`tests/test_restraints.py:119-140]`):
- The schedule monotonically decreases forces across fractions of staging intervals, concluding at zero force (`tests/test_restraints.py:124-131]`).

```mermaid
graph TD
    R[""parse_restraints()""] -->|"kind: position"| P[""Positional Restraints (kJ/mol/nm^2)""]
    R -->|"kind: distance"| D[""Distance Restraints (explicit force)""]
    R -->|"kind: torsion"| T[""Torsion Restraints (kJ/mol/rad^2)""]
    P & D & T -->|"managed by"| RS[""ReleaseSchedule.force_at(fraction)""]
    RS -->|"decays to 0.0"| U[""Unrestrained Production State""]

    classDef default fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px;
```
*Figure 3: Restraint parsing workflow and force attenuation managed by `ReleaseSchedule`.*

Sources: `tests/test_restraints.py:1-140]`, `src/fastmdxplora/simulation/restraints.py`

---

## 4. Telemetry, Checkpoints, and Seals

The runner emits progress and system states at strict intervals defined in step counts:
- Trajectory interval: `DEFAULT_TRAJECTORY_INTERVAL_STEPS` (`src/fastmdxplora/simulation/runner.py:120-120`)
- State interval: `DEFAULT_STATE_INTERVAL_STEPS` (`src/fastmdxplora/simulation/runner.py:121-121`)
- Checkpoint interval: `DEFAULT_CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL_STEPS` (`src/fastmdxplora/simulation/runner.py:122-122`)

### Checkpoint Seals and Interruption Detection
Checkpoint files (`checkpoint.chk`) preserve exact phase states for recovery. When executions are prematurely terminated (e.g., process crashes or manual interrupts), lack of a completion manifest or sealing record flags the segment as unsealed (`tests/test_a_study_stopped_twice_is_carried_on.py:93-107]`). The recovery engine isolates unsealed segments to protect downstream data integrity.

```mermaid
graph TD
    S[""Simulation Execution Loop""] -->|"every 10k steps"| C[""checkpoint.chk written""]
    S -->|"every 1k steps"| T[""Trajectory & State Reporters""]
    S -->|"Normal Completion"| M[""Manifest.json Sealed""]
    S -->|"Abrupt Interruption"| U[""Unsealed Segment / Missing Manifest""]
    U -->|"Handled by"| R[""resume_study() Engine""]

    classDef default fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px;
```
*Figure 4: Data flow for telemetry reporting, periodic checkpoints, and seal validation.*

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/simulation/runner.py:119-123]`, `tests/test_a_study_stopped_twice_is_carried_on.py:93-107]`

---

## 5. Stop Grace, Resume and Extension

To maximize hardware utilization, studies can be split into segments or extended dynamically, provided the underlying thermodynamic method permits it (`src/fastmdxplora/simulation/resume.py:1-41]`).

### Segmentability Evaluation
`segmentability()` evaluates whether a configuration can be safely split or resumed (`src/fastmdxplora/simulation/resume.py:102-110]`):
- **Metadynamics**: Refused for segmentation (`simulation.resume.bias_not_carried`), because PLUMED history files (`HILLS`) are required to preserve biasing states across resumes (`src/fastmdxplora/simulation/resume.py:112-120]`).
- **Steered MD**: Refused (`simulation.resume.time_dependent_bias`) because time-dependent moving restraints break when resumed mid-pull (`src/fastmdxplora/simulation/resume.py:122-130]`).
- **Unbiased Runs and Umbrella Windows**: Allowed; unbiased runs rely solely on checkpoint velocities and positions, while umbrella windows maintain coordinate-based restraints (`src/fastmdxplora/simulation/resume.py:132-158]`).

### Extension and Interrupted Segment Management
When a run is interrupted before an extension segment writes its first checkpoint, the resume framework (`resume_study` / `extend_study`) sets aside the corrupted segment (e.g., renaming it with `-stopped-before-its-checkpoint`) and resumes cleanly from the latest valid preceding checkpoint (`tests/test_a_study_stopped_before_its_extension_s_checkpoint_is_carried_on.py:85-110]`).

```mermaid
graph TD
    CFG[""Study Configuration""] --> S[""segmentability(config)""]
    S -->|"Metadynamics / Steered"| REF[""Refused: Bias State Lost""]
    S -->|"Unbiased / Umbrella"| ACC[""Allowed: Checkpoint Carry-over""]
    ACC --> K[""Interruption Check""]
    K -->|"Valid Checkpoint Found"| CONT[""extend_study() / resume_study()""]
    K -->|"Missing Checkpoint in Segment"| ASIDE[""Set Aside Corrupt Segment & Roll Back""]

    classDef default fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px;
```
*Figure 5: Decision tree for segmentability validation, interruption recovery, and study extension routines.*

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/simulation/resume.py:1-158]`, `tests/test_a_study_stopped_before_its_extension_s_checkpoint_is_carried_on.py:85-110]`, `tests/test_a_study_stopped_twice_is_carried_on.py:1-107]`

---
