## Purpose and Scope
This page details the implementation of the graphical user interface's core functional views within FastMDXplora: the schema-driven configuration builder (`run-builder.js` and `config_builder.py`), the live Overview telemetry dashboard (`overview_view.py`, `overview.js`, and `charts.js`), the aggregated Analysis page (`analysis_overview.py` and `analysis-page.js`), and the Report document page (`report_page.py` and `report-page.js`). These modules decouple the browser dashboard from hardcoded study templates, feeding structured payloads dynamically through backend validation loops and rendering canvas-based statistical plots and document objects.

---

## 1. Schema-Driven Config Builder Architecture
The configuration builder operates on a schema-first paradigm. Rather than maintaining static form fields in HTML or JavaScript, form controls, types, units, and boundary limits are fetched dynamically from backend schema registries (`fastmdxplora.config.schema`) via `schema_payload.py` [src/fastmdxplora/gui/schema_payload.py:1-18] and rendered client-side via `run-builder.js` [src/fastmdxplora/gui/static/run-builder.js:1-19]. 

User configurations are translated into validated YAML dictionaries through `config_builder.py` (`build_config`, `_coerce`, `_coerce_like`) [src/fastmdxplora/gui/config_builder.py:47-120] and validated using the CLI's shared validation harness (`validate_config`) [src/fastmdxplora/config/loader.py] to guarantee that invalid or incompatible configurations are intercepted in the browser prior to job submission.

```mermaid
graph TD
    sub5["Browser Client Space"]
    sub6["Backend Schema & Coercion Space"]
    
    sub5 -->|"/api/schema"| sub6
    sub6 -->|"schema_payload.py:schema_payload()"| sub5
    sub5 -->|"run-builder.js:state values"| sub6
    sub6 -->|"config_builder.py:build_config()"| sub6
    sub6 -->|"fastmdxplora.config.loader:validate_config()"| sub6
    sub6 -->|"Resolved Config YAML / Refusal Warning"| sub5

    classDef default fill:#fff,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px;
    class sub5,sub6 default;
```
*Figure 1: Data flow bridging the client-side form state in `run-builder.js` to backend validation and schema definitions in `schema_payload.py` and `config_builder.py`.*

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/gui/static/run-builder.js:1-115`, `src/fastmdxplora/gui/config_builder.py:33-120`, `src/fastmdxplora/gui/schema_payload.py:1-42`

---

## 2. Overview Dashboard and Telemetry Charts
The Overview page presents high-level study outcomes, thermodynamic metrics, and phase completion statuses. It aggregates findings via `overview_payload()` in `overview_view.py` [src/fastmdxplora/gui/overview_view.py:63-90] and plots time-series metrics through dependency-free HTML5 Canvas charts implemented in `charts.js` [src/fastmdxplora/gui/static/charts.js:1-40] coordinated with `overview.js` [src/fastmdxplora/gui/static/overview.js:1-16].

Key thermodynamic metrics (`potential_energy`, `total_energy`, `temperature`, `density`, and simulation speed) are tracked against the production clock (`clock.startNs`), where equilibration steps occurring prior to production are plotted prior to the $t=0$ axis [src/fastmdxplora/gui/static/charts.js:109-117].

```mermaid
graph TD
    sub7["overview_view.py:overview_payload()"]
    sub8["overview.js:renderTiles()"]
    sub9["charts.js:renderLatest()"]
    sub10["HTML5 Canvas Context"]

    sub7 -->|"/api/overview JSON Payload"| sub8
    sub7 -->|"/api/overview Thermodynamics Data"| sub9
    sub8 -->|"Tile DOM Elements & Sparklines"| sub10
    sub9 -->|"Metrics Canvas Drawing Loop"| sub10

    classDef default fill:#fff,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px;
    class sub7,sub8,sub9,sub10 default;
```
*Figure 2: Overview rendering pipeline from backend data generation to client canvas and tile insertion.*

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/gui/overview_view.py:63-90`, `src/fastmdxplora/gui/static/overview.js:75-110`, `src/fastmdxplora/gui/static/charts.js:50-96`

---

## 3. Analysis Page, Index, and Convergence
The Analysis page displays analysis outcomes, statistical means, error bounds, and convergence metrics. Backend aggregation is handled by `overview_of()` in `analysis_overview.py` [src/fastmdxplora/gui/analysis_overview.py:44-100], which reads analysis manifests (`analysis_manifest.json`) and individual option files (`options.json`) to extract quantitative findings, uncertainty bounds, sample sizes, and reweighted biased averages (`load_reweighted`) [src/fastmdxplora/gui/analysis_overview.py:77-83].

Client-side interaction, search-based section indexing, and convergence tracking under time-series plots are managed by `analysis-page.js` [src/fastmdxplora/gui/static/analysis-page.js:1-17].

```mermaid
graph TD
    sub11["analysis_overview.py:overview_of()"]
    sub12["analysis-page.js:sectionsRendered()"]
    sub13["DOM Analysis Index & Filters"]
    sub14["Convergence Estimator /statistics"]

    sub11 -->|"/api/analysis-overview"| sub12
    sub12 -->|"Filter Input Event Listeners"| sub13
    sub11 -->|"Mean Records & Findings"| sub14
    sub14 -->|"Running Mean & Block Averages"| sub12

    classDef default fill:#fff,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px;
    class sub11,sub12,sub13,sub14 default;
```
*Figure 3: Data architecture for analysis aggregation, indexing, and convergence payload generation.*

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/gui/analysis_overview.py:44-100`, `src/fastmdxplora/gui/static/analysis-page.js:84-133`

---

## 4. Report Generation, Methods Prose and Artifacts
The Report subsystem compiles study findings, methods prose, and artifact bundle locations into a unified document viewer. `report_payload()` in `report_page.py` [src/fastmdxplora/gui/report_page.py:22-85] parses `report/report.md`, checks for unproduced artifacts in `not_produced.json` [src/fastmdxplora/gui/report_page.py:45-56], maps relative figure paths (`_links_from_the_report`) [src/fastmdxplora/gui/report_page.py:116-156], and aggregates download targets for PDF, slides, bundles, and summary figures [src/fastmdxplora/gui/report_page.py:58-65].

Client-side UI components (`report-page.js`) render interactive dropdown menus for artifact downloads, handle browser print dialog fallbacks when `WeasyPrint` is absent, and manage unproduced warning banners [src/fastmdxplora/gui/static/report-page.js:1-162].

```mermaid

    sub18["DOM Report Viewer & Download Menu"]

    sub15 -->|"Markdown Source & not_produced.json"| sub16
    sub16 -->|"Resolved HTML & Artifact Paths"| sub17
    sub17 -->|"Download Dropdown & Notice Banners"| sub18

    classDef default fill:#fff,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px;
    class sub15,sub16,sub17,sub18 default;
```
*Figure 4: Report generation and artifact linking data flow.*

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/gui/report_page.py:22-85`, `src/fastmdxplora/gui/static/report-page.js:100-162`

The purpose of this page is to detail the technical mechanisms by which FastMDXplora launches, monitors, extends, repairs, and re-analyzes molecular dynamics studies directly from its zero-dependency localhost graphical user interface. The GUI relies on a conservative exploration layer that validates configurations and delegates heavy compute tasks to isolated child processes executing the standard `python -m fastmdxplora explore` workflow [src/fastmdxplora/gui/exploration.py:1-9]().

---

## 1. Exploration Lifecycle and Process Management

The runtime orchestration of studies initiated from the GUI is managed by `DashboardRuntime` in `src/fastmdxplora/gui/exploration.py`. Before any project directory is created or modified, the GUI validates configuration schemas against registry definitions [src/fastmdxplora/gui/exploration.py:35-46]().

When a user initiates a study configuration from the dashboard, `DashboardRuntime` cleans stale state flags [tests/test_exploration.py:41-66](), checks directory output constraints [tests/test_exploration.py:99-120](), and spawns a background child process running the `explore` command [tests/test_exploration.py:47-61]().

Process liveness and termination differ across platforms to avoid signal translation bugs (such as Windows handling `os.kill(pid, 0)` by terminating processes). The `_process_alive()` function checks platform-specific process states via ctypes/Windows API or POSIX signals without disturbing target workers [src/fastmdxplora/gui/exploration.py:88-122](). Graceful shutdowns (`stop()`) issue a termination signal and enforce a configurable timeout before escalating to forced cleanup [tests/test_exploration.py:122-153]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["UserAction: LaunchStudy"] --> B["DashboardRuntime.launch_from_config"]
    B --> C["prepare_run()"]
    C --> D["subprocess.Popen(fastmdxplora explore)"]
    D --> E["DashboardRuntime.snapshot()"]
    E --> F["LiveStatusWriter & Telemetry Poll"]

    subcode["Code Entity Space"]
    style subcode fill:none,stroke:none
    class A,B,C,D,E,F codeNode
    end
```
*Figure 1: Exploration Launch Lifecycle mapping dashboard triggers to process spawning routines.*

**Sources:** `src/fastmdxplora/gui/exploration.py:1-191`, `tests/test_exploration.py:41-153`

---

## 2. In-Place Study Extension and Segment Joining

When an MD study reaches its production duration limit or is interrupted, extending the study does not create a disjointed project; instead, it appends a numbered segment (`segment-001`, `segment-002`, etc.) within the same study container [tests/test_a_study_is_extended_in_place.py:1-48]().

The analysis package handles segment continuity via `fastmdxplora.analysis.joining`, which surveys existing directories, verifies completion flags from checkpoint sidecars, and validates study configurations using a robust digest function (`_config_digest`) that normalizes parameters varying by design (like `duration_ns` or `resume_from`) [src/fastmdxplora/analysis/joining.py:45-155]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["survey_segments()"] --> B["SegmentPiece objects"]
    B --> C{"Check Usability"}
    C -->|Unsealed / Gap Found| D["Raise MissingResultError / StudyError"]
    C -->|Clean Segments| E["_config_digest() verification"]
    E --> F["join_segments()"]
    F --> G["Concatenated DCD & .join.json"]

    subcode["Code Entity Space"]
    style subcode fill:none,stroke:none
    end
```
*Figure 2: Segment validation and joining pipeline mapping dataset discovery to integrity checks.*

Key safety refusals enforced during segment inspection include:
* **Gaps:** Missing intermediate segments (e.g., jumping from `segment-001` to `segment-003`) are refused to prevent silent physical discontinuities in downstream correlation analysis [src/fastmdxplora/analysis/joining.py:11-18]().
* **Unsealed checkpoints:** Segments lacking a proper sidecar completion flag are treated as incomplete crashes [src/fastmdxplora/analysis/joining.py:19-22]().
* **Dataset mismatch:** Segments originating from different force fields or non-identical resolved configurations are strictly rejected [src/fastmdxplora/analysis/joining.py:23-28]().

**Sources:** `src/fastmdxplora/analysis/joining.py:32-162`, `tests/test_a_study_is_extended_in_place.py:1-151`, `tests/test_the_pieces_go_back_together.py:34-152`

---

## 3. Fixes and Remediation Engine

When a study stops prematurely or encounters an error, the GUI surfaces actionable remediation routines via `fixes_payload` [tests/test_a_fix_is_run_when_asked.py:23-58](). 

The remediation engine evaluates failure codes stored in the phase manifest and matches them with programmatic fixes (such as executing `fastmdx resume` or rerunning umbrella windows) [tests/test_a_fix_is_run_when_asked.py:53-86](). 

* **Runnable Fixes:** Operations backed by automated CLI commands feature clear pricing metrics (e.g., estimated wall-clock time required to finish remaining frames) and execute via `DashboardRuntime.run_a_fix()` when confirmed by the user [tests/test_a_fix_is_run_when_asked.py:53-86]().
* **Manual Decisions:** Refusals requiring domain-specific human choices (e.g., parameter adjustments or missing dependencies) are surfaced as informational advisories and are blocked from automated execution [tests/test_a_fix_is_run_when_asked.py:60-63]().

**Sources:** `tests/test_a_fix_is_run_when_asked.py:1-161`

---

## 4. Re-running Analysis ("Analyze-Again")

Users can invoke re-analysis of existing trajectories from the GUI without overwriting or invalidating the underlying simulation records. 

The orchestrator `FastMDXplora` supports phase-isolated execution switches (`FASTMDX_DASHBOARD_ACTIVE`) that trigger `_dashboard_writer` to process selected phases (e.g., `["analysis", "report"]`) [tests/test_a_stopped_run_is_said_as_far_as_it_got.py:108-143](). During this process:
1. The simulation phase telemetry (`live_status.json`) remains untouched and preserves its historical state [tests/test_a_stopped_run_is_said_as_far_as_it_got.py:121]().
2. New analysis phase markers are written incrementally as workers complete metrics extraction [tests/test_a_stopped_run_is_said_as_far_as_it_got.py:129-135]().

**Sources:** `tests/test_a_stopped_run_is_said_as_far_as_it_got.py:108-143`

---

## 5. Files Page and Run Notices

The Files page provides a structured window into the run directory workspace. It exposes generated topologies (`topology.pdb`), trajectory chunks (`*.dcd`), configuration backups (`resolved_config.yml`), manifest logs (`manifest.json`), and join sidecars (`*.join.json`).

Run notices display real-time state badges driven by telemetry updates. These notices warn operators of unsealed checkpoints, convergence anomalies, or budget limit approach flags, bridging the gap between raw file persistence and high-level dashboard awareness.

**Sources:** `src/fastmdxplora/gui/exploration.py:156-186`, `src/fastmdxplora/analysis/joining.py:80-88`

---

## Purpose and Scope

This page provides a high-level overview of the AI interfaces in FastMDXplora, encompassing natural-language study generation via the built-in Agent and machine-protocol access via the Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. These interfaces allow external AI models, chat applications, and command-line users to translate natural language prompts or structured protocol requests into fully validated study configurations without bypassing core safety or chemical validation routines.

For deep technical details, see the child pages:
- [Agent Proposal Loop and Tools](#5.1)
- [Agent Panel in the GUI](#5.2)
- [MCP Server](#5.3)

Sources: [docs/agent.md:1-33](), [docs/mcp.md:1-20](), [src/fastmdxplora/agent/propose.py:1-41]()

---

## Natural Language Translation to Code Entities

The following diagram illustrates how natural-language instructions from a user or client application flow through the FastMDXplora agent subsystem, utilizing core schema validation and completion handlers.

```mermaid
graph TD
    NL[""Natural Language Prompt""] --> PC[""propose_config()""]
    subgraph "Agent Subsystem"
        PC --> AG[""fastmdxplora.agent.propose""]
        AG --> CF[""Completion Protocol""]
    end
    subgraph "Core Validation Space"
        AG --> VC[""validate_config()""]
        VC --> LE[""ConfigError / Refusal""]
        VC --> RC[""resolved_config.yml""]
    end
    RC --> EX[""fastmdxplora.explore""]

    classDef default fill:#fff,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px;
```

Title: Natural Language to Configuration Pipeline

Sources: [docs/agent.md:1-43](), [src/fastmdxplora/agent/propose.py:43-120]()

---

## 5.1 Agent Proposal Loop and Tools

The FastMDXplora Agent parses natural language requests into YAML configurations using a tightly bounded proposal and repair loop. Defined in `fastmdxplora.agent.propose`, the system relies on a `Completion` protocol to interface with various AI providers (such as Anthropic, OpenAI, or compatible local servers) `[src/fastmdxplora/agent/propose.py:65-75]()`. 

Every generated configuration must pass through the exact same deterministic validator (`validate_config`) used by the CLI and GUI `[docs/agent.md:35-52]()`. If validation fails, refusal codes are fed back into the repair loop up to a strict attempt ceiling. The agent also incorporates a toolbox (`fastmdxplora.agent.tools`) allowing models to inspect structures and review workspace states before drafting a proposal.

For details, see [Agent Proposal Loop and Tools](#5.1).

Sources: [src/fastmdxplora/agent/propose.py:1-120](), [docs/agent.md:1-65]()

---

## 5.2 Agent Panel in the GUI

The graphical user interface integrates the Agent via a dedicated panel (`agent-panel.js`) and corresponding backend endpoints (`model_endpoint`, `propose_endpoint`, `run_endpoint`) located in `fastmdxplora.gui.agent_panel` `[src/fastmdxplora/gui/static/agent-panel.js:1-60](), [src/fastmdxplora/gui/agent_panel.py:1-30]()`. 

The panel handles provider selection, API key management (stored server-side with strict file permissions to prevent client-side leakage), conversation threads, and records-based answering. It surfaces refusal messages directly to the user to aid configuration learning and provides live telemetry and context receipts.

For details, see [Agent Panel in the GUI](#5.2).

Sources: [src/fastmdxplora/gui/static/agent-panel.js:1-60](), [src/fastmdxplora/gui/agent_panel.py:1-35](), [tests/test_the_agent_panel.py:1-40]()

## Model Context Protocol (MCP) Routing Space

The following diagram details how external AI applications communicate with FastMDXplora over the Model Context Protocol (MCP), routing JSON-RPC method calls to application handlers and tool execution routines.

```mermaid
graph TD
    Client[""External AI App / Client""] -->|JSON-RPC over stdio| Server[""fastmdxplora.mcp.app.App.server()""]
    subgraph "Protocol Layer"
        Server --> Meth[""fastmdxplora.mcp.protocol.Server""]
        Meth --> Call[""Call Method Routing""]
    end
    subgraph "Tool Execution Space"
        Call --> ToolList[""TOOLS registry""]
        ToolList --> ToolRun[""Tool.run(Context, arguments)""]
        ToolRun --> Workspace[""Workspace Boundaries""]
    end

    classDef default fill:#fff,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px;
```

Title: Model Context Protocol Routing and Tool Execution

Sources: [src/fastmdxplora/mcp/app.py:73-116](), [src/fastmdxplora/mcp/protocol.py:1-50](), [src/fastmdxplora/mcp/tools.py:1-70]()

---

## 5.3 MCP Server

FastMDXplora includes a complete Model Context Protocol (MCP) server implementation (`fastmdxplora.mcp`) that exposes study orchestration, configuration checking, structure inspection, and workspace management to external AI applications (`docs/mcp.md:1-20`, `src/fastmdxplora/mcp/app.py:1-80`). 

Operating over standard input/output streams (`serve_stdio`), the MCP server enforces strict workspace boundaries (`Workspace`), handles protocol version negotiation (supporting both modern and legacy eras), and exposes a curated list of tools (`TOOLS`) and resources (guides and study records). All operations maintain the core safety invariant: no study can be saved or executed without passing the deterministic validator.

For details, see [MCP Server](#5.3).

Sources: [src/fastmdxplora/mcp/app.py:1-80](), [src/fastmdxplora/mcp/protocol.py:1-50](), [src/fastmdxplora/mcp/tools.py:1-40](), [docs/mcp.md:1-35]()

## Purpose and Scope
This page details the natural-language agent interface of FastMDXplora (`fastmdxplora.agent`). The agent subsystem translates high-level natural language user requests into valid study configuration files (`resolved_config.yml`) through an iterative proposal, validation, and repair loop. Crucially, the agent operates with **no special privileges**: every configuration generated by the AI model is checked by the exact same deterministic validator (`validate_config`) used by hand-written configurations or CLI invocations. 

This section covers implementation details for proposal cycles, the pre-answer inspection toolbox, conversation tool dispatch, provider abstraction, context receipts, and background worker queues.

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/agent/__init__.py:1-84`, `docs/agent.md:1-70`, `src/fastmdxplora/agent/propose.py:1-41` [src/fastmdxplora/agent/__init__.py:1-83](), [docs/agent.md:1-70](), [src/fastmdxplora/agent/propose.py:1-41]()

---

## 1. The Proposal Loop and Validation Retries

The core generation loop is managed by `propose_config` defined in `src/fastmdxplora/agent/propose.py`. A caller passes a textual prompt and a `Completion` callable (adhering to a simple protocol taking a prompt string and returning text). 

```mermaid
graph TD
    Prompt["Natural Language Prompt"] --> ProposeConfig["propose_config() src/fastmdxplora/agent/propose.py"]
    ProposeConfig --> LLM["Completion protocol src/fastmdxplora/agent/propose.py:65"]
    LLM --> RawText["Raw LLM Text / YAML"]
    RawText --> Validate["validate_config() src/fastmdxplora/config/loader.py"]
    
    Validate -->|Pass| Accepted["Proposal accepted (config dict)"]
    Validate -->|Refusal / ConfigError| CheckRefusal{"Refusal Kind?"}
    
    CheckRefusal -->|Structural| Retry["Repair Prompt & Retry (< max_cycles)"]
    CheckRefusal -->|Semantic| StopSemantic["Halt loop immediately (no retry)"]
    
    Retry --> LLM
    StopSemantic --> Refused["Proposal.refusal returned"]
```
*Figure 1: Natural Language Space to Code Entity Space for configuration proposal and validation routing.*

### Key Classes and Data Structures
- **`Completion` (Protocol)**: Declared at `src/fastmdxplora/agent/propose.py:65`, defines the interface `__call__(self, prompt: str) -> str`.
- **`Attempt` (Dataclass)**: Represents a single pass around the loop, tracking `number`, `raw` model output, parsed `config`, and any encountered `refusal` [src/fastmdxplora/agent/propose.py:77-90]().
- **`Proposal` (Dataclass)**: Represents the outcome of an asking session, holding the final `config`, tuples of `attempts`, a `refusal` object if failed, optional `question`, `answer`, `action`, and tool `looks` [src/fastmdxplora/agent/propose.py:98-155]().

### Refusal Philosophy and Repair Constraints
The proposal loop enforces strict safety boundaries:
1. **Structural vs. Semantic Refusals**: Structural errors (e.g., misspelled option names, incorrect type) yield retry prompts containing permitted schema values. Semantic errors (e.g., undetermined protonation states at a specific pH margin) halt the loop immediately because a retry would rely on model guessing rather than deterministic chemical rules [src/fastmdxplora/agent/propose.py:32-36]().
2. **Cycle Caps**: `max_cycles` restricts thrashing, preventing infinite loops or random mutation until invalid-but-parsing configurations pass [src/fastmdxplora/agent/propose.py:24-31]().

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/agent/propose.py:43-155`, `tests/test_a_proposal_is_refused_until_it_is_not.py:1-134` [src/fastmdxplora/agent/propose.py:43-155](), [tests/test_a_proposal_is_refused_until_it_is_not.py:1-134]()

---

## 2. Toolbox and Pre-Answer Inspections

Before final submission or during multi-turn conversations, the agent can inspect the local environment and structures using tools defined in `src/fastmdxplora/agent/tools.py`. 

### Tool Execution Contract
Tools are restricted strictly to **read-only operations** ("looks"). They never run, write, or start simulations. If a model response begins with `USE: <tool>` followed by YAML arguments, the tool executes and feeds its output back into the next AI prompt context.

```mermaid
graph TD
    AgentLLM["AI Model Completion"] --> CheckUse{"Starts with USE:?"}
    CheckUse -->|Yes| ParseTool["Parse tool name & YAML args src/fastmdxplora/agent/tools.py"]
    ParseTool --> RunTool["Execute Tool function (e.g. inspect_structure)"]
    RunTool --> RecordLook["Create Look record src/fastmdxplora/agent/tools.py:87"]
    RecordLook --> RePrompt["Append Look output to Prompt & Re-query LLM"]
    CheckUse -->|No| FinalAnswer["Process final study configuration"]
```
*Figure 2: Pre-answer tool inspection data flow.*

### Built-in Tools and Limits
- **`MOST_LOOKS`**: Capped at `4` look iterations per user prompt to prevent runaway exploration loops [src/fastmdxplora/agent/tools.py:66]().
- **`Look` (Dataclass)**: Tracks the `tool` name, `asked` parameters, `said` output string, and `ok` boolean flag [src/fastmdxplora/agent/tools.py:87-94]().
- **`LOOK_WORDS`**: Maps internal tool names (e.g., `inspect_structure`, `find_structure`, `read_docs`, `check_config`) to human-readable progress sentences shown in the UI (`fastmdx agent` or the GUI agent panel) [src/fastmdxplora/agent/tools.py:112-125]().

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/agent/tools.py:1-157` [src/fastmdxplora/agent/tools.py:1-157]()

---

## 3. Conversation Protocol and Tool Calls

When operating via modern LLM tool-calling APIs rather than plain text parsing, `src/fastmdxplora/agent/conversation.py` coordinates structured turns (`src/fastmdxplora/agent/turns.py`).

### Reply Tools and Actions
The AI model can invoke specific reply tools declared via `reply_specs()` [src/fastmdxplora/agent/conversation.py:44]():
- `propose_config`: Supplies the study configuration along with per-setting `reasons` explaining why each parameter was selected [src/fastmdxplora/agent/conversation.py:51-76]().
- `ask_person`: Prompts the user for ambiguous details (e.g., selecting among multiple PDB deposition entries) [src/fastmdxplora/agent/conversation.py:77-85]().
- `act`: Requests execution of actions defined in `ACTS` (e.g., `run`, `stop`, `open viewer`, `rerun windows`, `analyze again`) [src/fastmdxplora/agent/conversation.py:35-41, 86-103]().
- `show_scene`: Proposes 3D molecular visualization states (representations, colors, highlights) [src/fastmdxplora/agent/conversation.py:104-117]().

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/agent/conversation.py:1-121`, `src/fastmdxplora/agent/turns.py` [src/fastmdxplora/agent/conversation.py:1-121]()

---

##  4. Models, Providers, and Credentials

Model configuration, endpoint translation, and API key isolation are managed in `src/fastmdxplora/agent/models.py`.

### Security and Key Handling
1. **Never Stored in Studies**: API keys are stored in isolated configuration files (e.g., `$FASTMDXPLORA_CONFIG_DIR/model.json` or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/fastmdxplora/model.json`) with restricted permissions (`0600` on POSIX systems) [docs/agent.md:116-129](), [tests/test_the_agent_command.py:58-61](). Keys are **never** written into study configurations, manifests, or logs [tests/test_the_agent_command.py:47-54]().
2. **Environment Precedence**: Environment variables (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `FASTMDX_MODEL_API_KEY`) are always checked before reading stored credential files, allowing seamless CI/CD and cluster batch job execution [src/fastmdxplora/agent/models.py:20-23](), [tests/test_the_agent_command.py:88-106]().

### Supported Providers
`PROVIDERS` defines integrations for `anthropic`, `openai`, and `compatible` (supporting local or remote OpenAI chat-compatible servers like Ollama, vLLM, DeepSeek, and OpenRouter) [src/fastmdxplora/agent/models.py:67-117]().

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/agent/models.py:1-169`, `docs/agent.md:72-135`, `tests/test_the_agent_command.py:1-147` [src/fastmdxplora/agent/models.py:1-169](), [docs/agent.md:72-135](), [tests/test_the_agent_command.py:1-147]()

---

## 5. Context Receipts, Memory, and Workers

To track the provenance of agent sessions and background operations, FastMDXplora implements context receipts and queue workers.

- **Context Receipts (`src/fastmdxplora/agent/receipt.py`)**: Summarize what system state, tools, and previous turns informed a generated configuration.
- **Workers and Queues (`src/fastmdxplora/agent/worker.py`, `src/fastmdxplora/agent/queue.py`, `src/fastmdxplora/agent/run.py`)**: Handle asynchronous execution of agent-proposed studies, budget tracking (`Budget`), and staged execution (`StagedRun`) where system setup precedes cost estimation and full simulation.

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/agent/__init__.py:22-34`, `src/fastmdxplora/agent/receipt.py`, `src/fastmdxplora/agent/worker.py` [src/fastmdxplora/agent/__init__.py:22-34]()

---

## Purpose and Scope

The Agent Panel provides a natural-language conversation interface embedded within the FastMDXplora graphical user interface (`src/fastmdxplora/gui/static/agent-panel.js` [src/fastmdxplora/gui/static/agent-panel.js:1-17]()). It bridges human descriptions of molecular dynamics studies and structured configuration payloads, handles model selection and credential isolation (`src/fastmdxplora/gui/agent_panel.py` [src/fastmdxplora/gui/agent_panel.py:1-15]()), and supplies offline or model-free responses directly from analysis telemetry records (`src/fastmdxplora/gui/records_answer.py` [src/fastmdxplora/gui/records_answer.py:1-16]()).

---

## 1. Conversation UI and Side-Drawer Architecture

The frontend implementation consists of the core agent panel renderer (`src/fastmdxplora/gui/static/agent-panel.js` [src/fastmdxplora/gui/static/agent-panel.js:1-17]()) and the side drawer manager (`src/fastmdxplora/gui/static/agent-beside.js`), which allows the conversation interface to be overlaid beside any dashboard view via shortcut `Ctrl+J` or command buttons [tests/test_the_agent_opens_beside_any_page.py:1-7]().

### UI Components and Rendering Functions
- `prose(text)`: Sanitizes HTML special characters and parses limited markdown (`code`, bold, italic, and URLs) to prevent cross-site scripting while permitting clean formatting in chat responses [src/fastmdxplora/gui/static/agent-panel.js:72-91]().
- `cite(box, cites)`: Generates interactive citation chips linking conversational mentions to analysis figures on the Analysis page, surfacing mean values and withheld warnings directly from study records [src/fastmdxplora/gui/static/agent-panel.js:97-132]().
- `sceneSaid(scene)`: Translates structural representation suggestions (e.g., representation type, color, frame, superposition) into human-readable descriptions before execution via `/api/scenes` [src/fastmdxplora/gui/static/agent-panel.js:137-150]().

```
Sources:
- [src/fastmdxplora/gui/static/agent-panel.js:1-150]()
- [tests/test_the_agent_opens_beside_any_page.py:1-10]()
```

---

## 2. Server-Side Endpoints and Credential Safety

The GUI backend (`src/fastmdxplora/gui/agent_panel.py`) exposes thin wrapper functions around core agent infrastructure (`fastmdxplora.agent`). It enforces strict security guarantees regarding API keys.

### Core Endpoints

| Function Name | Route / Purpose | Implementation Details |
|---|---|---|
| `model_endpoint` | `/api/agent/model` | Reads or sets AI provider choices. Keys are saved in `$FASTMDXPLORA_CONFIG_DIR/model.json` with `0600` permissions and **never returned to the browser** [src/fastmdxplora/gui/agent_panel.py:34-83](). |
| `propose_endpoint` | `/api/agent/propose` | Accepts a natural-language request string, delegates to `propose_config()`, and returns validated configuration YAML alongside repair attempt history [src/fastmdxplora/gui/agent_panel.py:124-157](). |
| `run_endpoint` | `/api/agent/run` | Initiates simulation runs from proposed or modified configurations while relocating active conversations into the run folder [tests/test_a_conversation_follows_a_run_that_wrote_nothing.py:98-118](). |

### Security Property: Key Isolation
To prevent leakage via browser screenshots, extensions, or DOM inspection logs, `model_endpoint` never echoes stored API credentials back in JSON responses [tests/test_the_agent_panel.py:70-76]().

```python
# src/fastmdxplora/gui/agent_panel.py
def model_endpoint(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    ...
    save_choice(ModelChoice(provider, model, base_url), key=str(payload.get("api_key") or ""))
    # Returns choice metadata, omitting the secret key entirely
    return {"ok": True, "models": offered, "current": ModelChoice(provider, model, base_url).as_record()}
```

```
Sources:
- [src/fastmdxplora/gui/agent_panel.py:34-122]()
- [tests/test_the_agent_panel.py:55-98]()
```

## 3. Records-Based Fallback Answering

When no AI model is configured (or when users select quick study queries on the start page), FastMDXplora answers predefined questions (`found`, `long_enough`, `strengthen`) directly from simulation telemetry records using `src/fastmdxplora/gui/records_answer.py` [src/fastmdxplora/gui/records_answer.py:1-43]().

### Telemetry Queries Handled
1. **`found`**: Summarizes the report findings (`_supports`) and extracts analysis means, error bounds, effective sample sizes, and equilibration frames (`_means`) [src/fastmdxplora/gui/records_answer.py:56-121]().
2. **`long_enough`**: Evaluates convergence status and calculates exact nanosecond shortfalls (`sampling_asked_for`) with corresponding CLI resume commands [tests/test_the_agent_answers_from_the_records.py:69-80]().
3. **`strengthen`**: Recommends production extensions or replica seed sweeps based on statistical inefficiency metrics [tests/test_the_agent_answers_from_the_records.py:117-128]().

```
Sources:
- [src/fastmdxplora/gui/records_answer.py:1-54]()
- [tests/test_the_agent_answers_from_the_records.py:52-90]()
```

# MCP Server

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

- [tests/test_the_top_bars_are_one_height.py](tests/test_the_top_bars_are_one_height.py)

</details>



The purpose and scope of the FastMDXplora Model Context Protocol (MCP) server is to expose study orchestration, structural analysis, and remote machine control primitives via the Model Context Protocol standard (`docs/mcp.md:1-8`, `src/fastmdxplora/mcp/app.py:1-33`). This permits AI applications, coding agents, and automated chat interfaces to inspect molecular structures, validate configuration files against schema rules, initiate simulations locally or on remote targets, and review telemetry without bypassing validation checks or file system workspace constraints (`docs/mcp.md:9-20`, `src/fastmdxplora/mcp/app.py:35-70`).

---

## 1. Protocol Handling and Application Server

The core MCP application is implemented in `src/fastmdxplora/mcp/app.py`, which wraps protocol routing logic from `src/fastmdxplora/mcp/protocol.py`. The `App` class configures method dispatch mappings for JSON-RPC operations such as `tools/list`, `tools/call`, `prompts/list`, `prompts/get`, `resources/list`, and `resources/read` (`src/fastmdxplora/mcp/app.py:73-117`).

```mermaid
graph TD
    Client["AIAppClient"] -->|"JSON-RPC Request"| Protocol["src/fastmdxplora/mcp/protocol.py:Server"]
    Protocol -->|"Route Method"| AppInstance["src/fastmdxplora/mcp/app.py:App"]
    AppInstance -->|"tools/list"| ListTools["src/fastmdxplora/mcp/app.py:_list_tools"]
    AppInstance -->|"tools/call"| CallTool["src/fastmdxplora/mcp/app.py:_call_tool"]
    CallTool -->|"Execute"| ToolObj["src/fastmdxplora/mcp/tools.py:Tool"]
    AppInstance -->|"resources/read"| ReadRes["src/fastmdxplora/mcp/content.py:read_resource"]

    classDef default fill:none,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px;
```
*Figure 1: MCP Server request routing architecture linking protocol handlers to application tools.*

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/mcp/app.py:73-117`, `src/fastmdxplora/mcp/protocol.py:1-120`

---

## 2. Exposed Tools and Workspace Isolation

Tools are defined in `src/fastmdxplora/mcp/tools.py` using the `Tool` dataclass. Each tool receives a `Context` instance containing the `Workspace` reference, call metadata, and an execution flag (`runs: bool`) determining whether state-modifying actions are permitted (`src/fastmdxplora/mcp/tools.py:48-70`).

Workspace boundaries are strictly enforced. All file reading, config generation, and study initialization must occur inside the designated workspace root (`src/fastmdxplora/mcp/workspace.py`). Paths crossing outside via `..` or symbolic links are caught and refused with `ToolError` (`src/fastmdxplora/mcp/tools.py:129-142`).

```mermaid
graph TD
    NLSpace["NaturalLanguageQuery: check_study or start_study"] -->|"Arguments Dict"| ToolChecked["src/fastmdxplora/mcp/tools.py:Tool.checked"]
    ToolChecked -->|"Validate Schema"| WorkspaceBound["src/fastmdxplora/mcp/workspace.py:Workspace.inside"]
    WorkspaceBound -->|"Path Safe?"| RunLogic["src/fastmdxplora/mcp/tools.py:Tool.run"]
    RunLogic -->|"Success / ToolError"| ResultFormat["src/fastmdxplora/mcp/app.py:_call_tool"]

    classDef default fill:none,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px;
```
*Figure 2: Natural language input mapping to validated code entities in the MCP tool subsystem.*

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/mcp/tools.py:32-111`, `src/fastmdxplora/mcp/workspace.py:1-100`

---

## 3. Prompts, Resources, and Content Types

Content types, prompt templates, and virtual resources are managed in `src/fastmdxplora/mcp/content.py`. The server registers templates matching `fastmdxplora://` URIs, enabling AI apps to read configuration guides, working-with-studies specifications, and active study manifests directly (`src/fastmdxplora/mcp/app.py:93-112`).

The server provides predefined prompts via `prompts/list` and `prompts/get` which instruct models on proper protocol behavior, refusing unvalidated settings, and requesting structural parameters (`src/fastmdxplora/mcp/app.py:100-103`).

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/mcp/content.py:1-150`, `src/fastmdxplora/mcp/app.py:88-117`

---

## 4. Remote Tools and Cross-Machine Control

When operating in active mode (`runs=True`), remote execution tools defined in `src/fastmdxplora/mcp/remote_tools.py` bridge AI application requests to other compute resources via `src/fastmdxplora/mcp/remote_tools.py` and `src/fastmdxplora/remote/api.py` (`src/fastmdxplora/mcp/remote_tools.py:1-37`).

Key safeguards implemented in remote tooling include:
- **Explicit Confirmation**: Studies are dispatched to remote workstations or clusters only after explicit approval context is confirmed, preventing unsupervised execution (`src/fastmdxplora/mcp/remote_tools.py:10-15`).
- **GPU Memory Accounting**: Workstation deployments query GPU utilization and free VRAM using `gpu_room` calculations before transmitting files (`src/fastmdxplora/remote/gpu_room.py:1-42`).
- **Fetch Size Limits**: Unasked data retrieval is bounded by `LARGE_BYTES` (100 MB), forcing manual confirmation for large trajectory bundles (`src/fastmdxplora/mcp/remote_tools.py:39-47`).

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/mcp/remote_tools.py:1-155`, `src/fastmdxplora/remote/api.py:1-100`

---

# Page: Remote Execution

# Remote Execution

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [docs/api.md](docs/api.md)
- [docs/remote.md](docs/remote.md)
- [src/fastmdxplora/mcp/remote_tools.py](src/fastmdxplora/mcp/remote_tools.py)
- [src/fastmdxplora/remote/api.py](src/fastmdxplora/remote/api.py)
- [src/fastmdxplora/remote/gpu_room.py](src/fastmdxplora/remote/gpu_room.py)
- [src/fastmdxplora/remote/send.py](src/fastmdxplora/remote/send.py)
- [tests/test_remote_from_every_interface.py](tests/test_remote_from_every_interface.py)

</details>



Studies are often designed locally on laptops or workstations and executed on dedicated GPU lab servers or high-performance computing clusters [docs/remote.md:1-6](). FastMDXplora provides a remote execution subsystem reachable through the command line (`fastmdx remote`), the Python API (`fastmdxplora.remote.api`), model-context-protocol tools (`fastmdxplora.mcp.remote_tools`), and the localhost graphical dashboard [docs/remote.md:4](), [src/fastmdxplora/mcp/remote_tools.py:1-18](), [src/fastmdxplora/remote/api.py:1-24](). Remote execution handles machine inspection, environment probing, version parity verification, automated installation plans, input safety checks, dynamic VRAM allocation, file transfer, and job telemetry retrieval [docs/remote.md:8-17](), [src/fastmdxplora/remote/send.py:1-46]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Natural Language / CLI Space"
    A["fastmdx remote --machine gpu-box"] --> B["Inspection & Probe"]
    C["fastmdx remote send -c study.yml"] --> D["Plan & GPU Fit"]
    end
    subgraph "Code Entity Space"
    B --> E["src/fastmdxplora/remote/probe.py"]
    E --> F["src/fastmdxplora/remote/machines.py"]
    D --> G["src/fastmdxplora/remote/send.py"]
    G --> H["src/fastmdxplora/remote/gpu_room.py"]
    G --> I["src/fastmdxplora/remote/transport.py"]
    end
    style A stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style C stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style E stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style G stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
```
*Diagram 1: Bridging remote execution commands to underlying modules [docs/remote.md:13-15](), [src/fastmdxplora/remote/send.py:70-116]().*

Sources: `docs/remote.md:1-24`, `src/fastmdxplora/remote/send.py:1-46`, `src/fastmdxplora/remote/api.py:1-24`.

---

## 6.1. Machines, Probing and Installation

Remote machines are registered and inspected via standard `ssh` configurations (`~/.ssh/config` aliases or `user@host` specifications) [docs/remote.md:28-29](). Inspection scripts read-only evaluate target hosts for hardware (CPUs, system memory, and NVIDIA GPU drivers), Python environments (conda/mamba/micromamba installations holding `fastmdx`), container runtimes (Apptainer), and job schedulers (SLURM) [docs/remote.md:53-65](). 

Readiness requires strict commit parity or release version matching: the remote installation must contain the identical codebase and dependencies to ensure configuration defaults resolve consistently [docs/remote.md:71-75](). When a target is unready, the framework generates a precise **install plan** enumerating non-privileged environment creation commands or `git` commit merging actions restricted strictly to the user account [docs/remote.md:109-156]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Code Entity Space"
    J["fastmdxplora.remote.api.machines()"] --> K["fastmdxplora.remote.machines.load_machine"]
    K --> L["fastmdxplora.remote.machines.readiness"]
    L --> M["fastmdxplora.remote.installer.install"]
    end
    style J stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style M stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
```
*Diagram 2: Machine loading and inspection function pathways [src/fastmdxplora/remote/api.py:92-107](), [src/fastmdxplora/remote/machines.py:108-114]().*

For detailed documentation on machine records, SSH transport options, probe scripts, readiness parity checks, install plans, job tracking, and cluster schedulers, see [Machines, Probing and Installation](#6.1).

Sources: `docs/remote.md:26-165`, `src/fastmdxplora/remote/api.py:92-120`, `src/fastmdxplora/remote/machines.py:108-114`.

---

## 6.2. Planning, Inputs Safety and GPU Allocation

Before any file transfer occurs, local configuration files undergo strict validation and planning [src/fastmdxplora/remote/send.py:13-15](). Workspace boundaries (`gather_inputs`) ensure that only files within the study's own directory structure travel across the transport link, blocking accidental leakage of private paths or parent directories [src/fastmdxplora/remote/send.py:17-19](), [src/fastmdxplora/remote/gpu_room.py:1-9]().

On multi-GPU workstations, studies dynamically share hardware resources without manual device assignment [src/fastmdxplora/remote/send.py:21-25](). VRAM accounting is managed through `gpu_room.py`, which evaluates current GPU memory usage via `nvidia-smi`, tracks historical process memory footprints, and applies a safety margin (`MARGIN = 1.15`) before dispatching jobs via `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` [src/fastmdxplora/remote/gpu_room.py:1-48](). Cluster environments bypass local VRAM heuristics, relying instead on scheduler-allocated nodes (e.g., `sbatch`) [src/fastmdxplora/remote/send.py:29-30](), [src/fastmdxplora/remote/gpu_room.py:23-24]().

For detailed coverage of `gather_inputs` boundary enforcement, private-path blocking, plan tokens, and VRAM fitting algorithms, see [Planning, Inputs Safety and GPU Allocation](#6.2).

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/remote/send.py:1-46`, `src/fastmdxplora/remote/gpu_room.py:1-48`.

---

## 6.3. Remote from the GUI

The graphical user interface and AI integration tiers expose remote execution capabilities through dedicated web routes and automated API agents [src/fastmdxplora/mcp/remote_tools.py:1-18](). The dashboard server maintains non-blocking asynchronous wrappers around remote operations, polling job states at controlled intervals (at most every 30 seconds) to prevent remote daemon saturation [src/fastmdxplora/remote/send.py:36-39]().

Users can inspect machines, view live job telemetry, and execute plan-send-fetch-cancel workflows directly from the browser shell (`remote.js`) or via Model Context Protocol tools (`remote_tools.py`) [src/fastmdxplora/mcp/remote_tools.py:1-18](). Safety guardrails require explicit human confirmation for file dispatch and regulate the automatic retrieval of large output bundles [src/fastmdxplora/mcp/remote_tools.py:10-15]().

For detailed documentation on `RemoteDesk` HTTP routing, dashboard frontend views, and interactive job management workflows, see [Remote from the GUI](#6.3).

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/mcp/remote_tools.py:1-18`, `src/fastmdxplora/remote/send.py:36-40`.

---

## Purpose and Scope

This page documents the remote execution architecture of FastMDXplora. It covers how external target machines (workstations, login nodes, and clusters) are modeled, inspected via low-overhead probe scripts, evaluated for code-parity readiness, provisioned with safe non-root install plans, and managed through automated VRAM resource allocation (`gpu_room`), secure SSH transports, and persistent job tracking.

Sources: `docs/remote.md:1-24` [docs/remote.md:1-24](), `src/fastmdxplora/remote/send.py:1-46` [src/fastmdxplora/remote/send.py:1-46](), `src/fastmdxplora/remote/api.py:1-24` [src/fastmdxplora/remote/api.py:1-24]()

---

## Machine Records and SSH Transport

FastMDXplora does not bundle or implement its own SSH client stack. Instead, it delegates all remote transport to the user's native system `ssh` and `rsync` binaries via `[src/fastmdxplora/remote/transport.py:1-20]()`. This ensures that local configuration directives in `~/.ssh/config` (such as `ProxyJump`, custom keys, certificates, or `Match` blocks) apply identically to automated study transfers.

### Machine Records

Machines are registered locally per user account in user configuration directories rather than embedded within study definitions [src/fastmdxplora/remote/machines.py:1-14](). Each record corresponds to an SSH alias and serializes the state captured during the last inspection.

The `Machine` class [src/fastmdxplora/remote/machines.py:55-64]() maintains structural metadata:
* `name`: The machine's SSH alias or target specifier [src/fastmdxplora/remote/machines.py:59]() (validated by `check_machine_name` in `[src/fastmdxplora/remote/transport.py:55-65]()`).
* `inspected_at`: UTC timestamp string of the survey [src/fastmdxplora/remote/machines.py:60]().
* `inspection`: An `Inspection` object detailing hardware topologies (CPUs, RAM, GPUs, scratch space) [src/fastmdxplora/remote/machines.py:61]().
* `info`: A dictionary mapping python/conda environment paths to output dictionaries from `fastmdx info --json` [src/fastmdxplora/remote/machines.py:62-64]().

```mermaid
title "Transport and Machine Record Architecture"

graph TD
    UserCLI["FastMDXplora CLI / API"] --> LoadMach["load_machine(name)<br/>src/fastmdxplora/remote/machines.py"]
    LoadMach --> MacRecord["Machine Record<br/>src/fastmdxplora/remote/machines.py"]
    MacRecord --> TransInit["Transport(name, interactive=False)<br/>src/fastmdxplora/remote/transport.py"]
    TransInit --> SSHExec["subprocess.run(ssh ...)<br/>src/fastmdxplora/remote/transport.py"]
    SSHExec --> RemoteHost["Remote Host / Cluster Node"]
    
    subgraph "Local User Storage"
        MacRecord
    end
```
Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/remote/machines.py:1-81` [src/fastmdxplora/remote/machines.py:1-81](), `src/fastmdxplora/remote/transport.py:1-140` [src/fastmdxplora/remote/transport.py:1-140]()

### SSH Transport Optimization

To prevent multi-prompt hangs (especially on multi-hop or MFA-protected clusters), the `Transport` class [src/fastmdxplora/remote/transport.py:107-128]() implements session reuse and non-interactive hardening:
* **Batch Mode**: When `interactive=False`, `BatchMode=yes` is enforced via SSH options to cause immediate failure on password/second-factor prompts instead of locking execution [src/fastmdxplora/remote/transport.py:132-133]().
* **Control Master Sockets**: Unix domain sockets are established under `user_config_dir() / "sockets"` or `/tmp` with restricted permissions (`0o700`) to maintain an active connection persist window (`ControlMaster=auto`, `ControlPersist=600`) [src/fastmdxplora/remote/transport.py:80-104, 135-139]().

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/remote/transport.py:80-165` [src/fastmdxplora/remote/transport.py:80-165]()

---

## Probing, Code Identity, and Readiness

Inspecting a machine reads hardware characteristics and validates environment configurations without modifying remote states `[docs/remote.md:53-56]()`. 

### Probe Scripts and Environments

Remote introspection is executed via bundled shell probe scripts (`PROBE_SCRIPT` in `[src/fastmdxplora/remote/probe.py]`). The inspection scans:
* CPU architecture, total memory, and GPU hardware (including NVIDIA driver capabilities and CUDA version ceilings) `[docs/remote.md:39-40]()`.
* Python/Conda installations (`conda`, `mamba`, `micromamba`) across user and system paths `[docs/remote.md:41, 57-62]()`.
* Container runtimes like Apptainer and pre-built SIF release images `[docs/remote.md:63]()`.
* Cluster scheduler presence (SLURM partitions) and scratch availability `[docs/remote.md:64-65]()`.

### Readiness and Commit Parity

A target machine is considered **ready** only if a specific remote installation contains code identical to the local controlling computer and successfully loads all scientific backends `[docs/remote.md:71-74]`.

The required core backends are defined in `REQUIRED_BACKENDS` `[src/fastmdxplora/remote/machines.py:46-47]()`:
```python
REQUIRED_BACKENDS = ("openmm", "pdbfixer", "openff.toolkit",
                     "openmmforcefields", "rdkit", "propka", "am1bcc")
```
For source checkouts, code parity is evaluated by matching **Git commits** and asserting that the working tree has no uncommitted changes `[docs/remote.md:78-84]()`. If an editable install version string diverges from the active commit hash, execution is halted to prevent schema or default divergence.

Sources: `docs/remote.md:39-85` [docs/remote.md:39-85](), `src/fastmdxplora/remote/machines.py:43-48` [src/fastmdxplora/remote/machines.py:43-48]()

---

## Install Plans and Confirmation

When a target machine lacks the correct environment or code commit, `fastmdx remote install` generates a deterministic **Install Plan** `[docs/remote.md:109-113]()`. 

### Safety and Non-Root Isolation

Install plans guarantee account-level isolation:
* No `sudo` privileges are requested or utilized `[docs/remote.md:136]()`.
* No modifications are written to shell startup profiles (`.bashrc`, `.zshrc`) `[docs/remote.md:136]()`.
* Separate version-specific conda environments (e.g., `fastmdx-2.5.6`) are provisioned so newer dependencies never break older studies `[docs/remote.md:137-138]()`.
* **CUDA Version Pinning**: `cuda-version` is explicitly pinned to match the driver's maximum supported CUDA version (or `12.6`), preventing runtime `CUDA_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_PTX_VERSION` faults `[docs/remote.md:131-134]()`.

### Confirmation and Token Security

The `install` function in `[src/fastmdxplora/remote/installer.py:68-76]()` enforces strict human-in-the-loop confirmation:
```python
def install(name: str, *, confirm: Callable[[InstallPlan], bool],
            transport: Transport | None = None,
            code: CodeIdentity | None = None,
            local_runner=None) -> InstallOutcome:
```
For non-terminal interfaces (such as GUIs or AI agent MCP servers), authorization is mediated through short-lived cryptographic tokens generated by `plan_yes()` and verified by `confirmed_by()` in `[src/fastmdxplora/remote/installer.py:160-175]()`. These tokens bind directly to a hashed representation of the exact install plan (`plan_digest()`), expiring after 10 minutes (`PLAN_YES_S = 600`) `[src/fastmdxplora/remote/installer.py:54, 140-146]()`.

Sources: `docs/remote.md:109-165` [docs/remote.md:109-165](), `src/fastmdxplora/remote/installer.py:1-122` [src/fastmdxplora/remote/installer.py:1-122]()

---

## Sending Studies, VRAM Allocation and GPU Room

Once a machine is confirmed ready, studies are transferred and executed. Transfer semantics isolate inputs and manage hardware contention.

### Input Safety and Transfer

Only the study's active configuration and local input dependencies under `inputs/` are bundled and sent via `rsync` `[src/fastmdxplora/remote/send.py:3-7]()`. Symbolic links are resolved prior to copying, and paths referencing sensitive parent directories are blocked.

### Workstation GPU Sharing and VRAM Accounting

When targeting local workstations (as opposed to managed clusters running SLURM), multiple studies share available GPUs `[src/fastmdxplora/remote/send.py:21-25]()`. 

The GPU room subsystem (`[src/fastmdxplora/remote/gpu_room.py:1-24]()`) dynamically tracks VRAM utilization:
* **Probe Query**: `GPU_SCRIPT` executes `nvidia-smi` to query GPU indices, UUIDs, total/free memory, and active compute applications mapped to process groups `[src/fastmdxplora/remote/gpu_room.py:63-76]()`.
* **Empirical Cost Learning**: Rather than relying on static estimates, past simulation runs record their memory footprint and particle count in `cost.json` `[src/fastmdxplora/remote/gpu_room.py:11-13]()`.
* **Safety Margin**: Required VRAM is calculated via historical fits scaled by a safety margin factor (`MARGIN = 1.15`) `[src/fastmdxplora/remote/gpu_room.py:47-48]()`.
* **Pinning**: Studies are assigned to the GPU with the fewest concurrent local jobs and the most free memory, locked via `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` set to the GPU's UUID `[src/fastmdxplora/remote/gpu_room.py:5-7]()`.

```mermaid
title "GPU Room Evaluation and Workload Placement"

graph TD
    SendReq["prepare() / send() request<br/>src/fastmdxplora/remote/send.py"] --> RunGPUQuery["GPU_SCRIPT execution via SSH<br/>src/fastmdxplora/remote/gpu_room.py"]
    RunGPUQuery --> ParseRoom["room_from(found)<br/>src/fastmdxplora/remote/gpu_room.py"]
    ParseRoom --> CalcNeed["need_for(study)<br/>src/fastmdxplora/remote/gpu_room.py"]
    CalcNeed --> FitCheck{"GPUs have sufficient<br/>VRAM + 15% margin?"}
    FitCheck -- "Yes" --> PinGPU["Select optimal GPU & pin<br/>CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=UUID"]
    FitCheck -- "No" --> RefuseSend["Refuse send with deficit metrics<br/>src/fastmdxplora/remote/send.py"]
    PinGPU --> RsyncCopy["Rsync inputs/ and Config<br/>src/fastmdxplora/remote/send.py"]
```
Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/remote/send.py:1-46` [src/fastmdxplora/remote/send.py:1-46](), `src/fastmdxplora/remote/gpu_room.py:1-78` [src/fastmdxplora/remote/gpu_room.py:1-78]()

---

## Job Tracking, Lifecycle, and Retrieval

To ensure durability across terminal closures or client disconnections, remote studies execute as detached background processes within isolated process groups on workstations, or as managed batch jobs (`sbatch`) on clusters `[src/fastmdxplora/remote/send.py:41-43]()`.

### Job Records and States

Job metadata is recorded locally in `user_config_dir() / "jobs/"` as standalone JSON files `[src/fastmdxplora/remote/jobs.py:41-44]()`. 

The lifecycle states mirror standard scheduler terminology (`[src/fastmdxplora/remote/jobs.py:33-38]()`):
* `ready`: Waiting in queue or unallocated.
* `running`: Actively executing simulation/analysis phases.
* `done`: Completed successfully with valid exit codes (`exit_code` written remotely).
* `failed`: Terminated with errors.
* `abandoned`: Cancelled or orphaned.

### Concurrency and File Locking

Because AI agent orchestrators and GUI servers frequently query job statuses asynchronously via threads, job record modifications are strictly serialized using thread-local reentrant locks (`held()` in `[src/fastmdxplora/remote/jobs.py:101-109]`). Atomic file writes utilize temporary scratch files (`tempfile.mkstemp`) followed by `os.replace` to eliminate partial read races `[src/fastmdxplora/remote/jobs.py:112-125]`.

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/remote/send.py:41-46` [src/fastmdxplora/remote/send.py:41-46](), `src/fastmdxplora/remote/jobs.py:1-110` [src/fastmdxplora/remote/jobs.py:1-110]()

---

This page covers the pre-flight planning, input security boundaries, cryptographic fingerprinting, and GPU memory accounting subsystems utilized when sending FastMDXplora studies to remote target machines or workstations (`src/fastmdxplora/remote/send.py:1-46`, `src/fastmdxplora/remote/inputs.py:1-32`, `src/fastmdxplora/remote/gpu_room.py:1-24`).

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/remote/send.py:1-46`, `src/fastmdxplora/remote/inputs.py:1-32`, `src/fastmdxplora/remote/gpu_room.py:1-24`

---

## 1. Input Gathering and Workspace Boundaries (`gather_inputs`)

When a study configuration is prepared for remote execution, FastMDXplora does not blindly copy the local file system structure. Instead, the configuration is parsed, and every string referencing an existing local file or directory is intercepted and re-mapped under an isolated `inputs/` directory in the remote workspace (`src/fastmdxplora/remote/inputs.py:1-13`).

### Implementation and Data Flow
The core logic resides in `gather_inputs` and supporting validators within `src/fastmdxplora/remote/inputs.py`. It traverses the configuration dictionary, ignoring configuration keys explicitly designated as results output paths (e.g., `_NOT_INPUTS = frozenset({"output"})`, `src/fastmdxplora/remote/inputs.py:53-54`) or words/selections (`word_keys()`, `src/fastmdxplora/remote/inputs.py:95-105`).

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph Natural Language Space
        A["User Declares Study Config"] --> B["Identify Paths in Config"]
    end
    subgraph Code Entity Space
        B --> C["gather_inputs(config, base_dir)"]
        C --> D["_existing(value, base)"]
        D --> E["_walked(path)"]
        E --> F["Inputs DataClass Object"]
    end
    F --> G["Map Files Under inputs/"]

    classDef default stroke:#000,fill:#fff;
```
*Figure 1: Natural Language to Code Entity mapping for input preparation.*

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/remote/inputs.py:1-118`

---

## 2. Private-Path Blocking and Security Rules

To prevent accidental data leaks or unauthorized file transfers (e.g., uploading private SSH keys, cloud credentials, or system configurations), strict refusal rules are enforced during input resolution (`src/fastmdxplora/remote/inputs.py:17-32`).

### Key Safety Checks
- **Home Folder and Root Protection:** Files located at or above the user's home directory or system root when expressed via unconstrained absolute paths are refused (`refuse_home_or_above`, `src/fastmdxplora/remote/inputs.py:50`).
- **Sensitive Credential Directories:** Folders containing sensitive credentials such as `.ssh`, `.gnupg`, `.aws`, or FastMDXplora configuration spaces trigger an immediate refusal error if encountered anywhere within a directory traversal (`src/fastmdxplora/remote/inputs.py:29-31`).
- **Symlink Escape Checks:** Symlinks pointing outside the study folder, or recursive links pointing back into the folder, are detected and blocked by `_walked(path)` to prevent infinite copy loops or path traversal attacks (`src/fastmdxplora/remote/inputs.py:140-165`).

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph Natural Language Space
        H["Check Target Path"] --> I["Is Path Sensitive? (.ssh, .aws)"]
        H --> J["Does Symlink Escape Study Folder?"]
    end
    subgraph Code Entity Space
        I --> K["refuse_kept_place(path)"]
        J --> L["link_out_of(path, base)"]
        K --> M["Raise StudyError"]
        L --> M
    end

    classDef default stroke:#000,fill:#fff;
```
*Figure 2: Security refusal pipeline routing unsafe paths to exceptions.*

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/remote/inputs.py:17-51`, `src/fastmdxplora/remote/inputs.py:140-165`

---

## 3. Cryptographic Fingerprints and Plan Tokens

To ensure that a user's approval of a remote send operation in the GUI or via API is cryptographically bound to the exact file bytes reviewed, FastMDXplora uses SHA-256 hashing (`src/fastmdxplora/gui/remote_routes.py:51-87`, `src/fastmdxplora/remote/send.py:50-50`).

### Fingerprints and Tokens
- **File Hashing (`_read_whole` & `_sha_of`):** Every regular file slated for transfer is read via non-blocking, non-following descriptors (`os.open` with `O_NOFOLLOW`) to compute a stable SHA-256 digest alongside device and inode metadata (`src/fastmdxplora/gui/remote_routes.py:51-85`).
- **Plan Tokens:** When a plan is generated (`plan_send`, `src/fastmdxplora/remote/api.py:125-138`), a unique time-limited token (`PLAN_KEPT_S = 600`, `src/fastmdxplora/gui/remote_routes.py:35-36`) is issued. Executing `send_planned` or submitting via GUI route requires matching this token and verifying that the underlying file digests remain unaltered (`src/tests/test_the_gui_reaches_your_machines.py:111-132`).

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph Natural Language Space
        N["User Requests Send Plan"] --> O["Inspect Config and Input Files"]
    end
    subgraph Code Entity Space
        O --> P["_read_whole(path)"]
        P --> Q["_sha_of(path)"]
        Q --> R["_Plan(config, machine, output, digest, made_at)"]
        R --> S["Issued Token Validated by RemoteDesk"]
    end

    classDef default stroke:#000,fill:#fff;
```
*Figure 3: Plan generation and token validation flow.*

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/gui/remote_routes.py:35-103`, `src/fastmdxplora/remote/api.py:125-138`

---

## 4. GPU VRAM Accounting and Learning (`gpu_room`)

When studies are dispatched to shared local workstations rather than managed cluster queues (like SLURM), FastMDXplora dynamically accounts for and allocates available GPU VRAM (`src/fastmdxplora/remote/gpu_room.py:1-24`).

### Mechanics of GPU Room
- **Hardware Probing (`GPU_SCRIPT`):** The remote workstation is queried via `nvidia-smi` commands formatted in `GPU_SCRIPT` to extract GPU indices, UUIDs, total/free memory, and active compute applications mapped to process groups (`src/fastmdxplora/remote/gpu_room.py:63-76`).
- **Empirical Learning (`cost.json`):** Memory requirements are not hardcoded guesses; each completed run outputs performance metrics and memory footprints into `cost.json`. The subsystem calculates expected memory requirements based on system particle size and precision, scaling it by a safety margin (`MARGIN = 1.15`, `src/fastmdxplora/remote/gpu_room.py:47-48`).
- **Device Selection (`choose`):** The placement algorithm inspects available GPUs, penalizing devices already running tasks from the current user, and selects the device maximizing free memory while respecting `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` constraints (`src/fastmdxplora/remote/gpu_room.py:3-9`, `src/fastmdxplora/remote/send.py:21-29`).

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph Natural Language Space
        T["Select Target Workstation"] --> U["Query GPU VRAM Status"]
    end
    subgraph Code Entity Space
        U --> V["GPU_SCRIPT via nvidia-smi"]
        V --> W["room_from(found)"]
        W --> X["need_for(study) using cost.json"]
        X --> Y["choose(room, need) -> Selected GPU UUID"]
        Y --> Z["Pin via CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES"]
    end

    classDef default stroke:#000,fill:#fff;
```
*Figure 4: GPU room analysis and device selection pipeline.*

### GPU Room Data Structures

| Class Name | Module Path | Role & Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Gpu` | `src/fastmdxplora/remote/gpu_room.py:80-91` | Represents an individual physical GPU device instance (index, UUID, total/free VRAM, core utilization). |
| `App` | `src/fastmdxplora/remote/gpu_room.py:94-104` | Tracks a compute process running on a specific GPU, storing process group IDs and allocated VRAM. |
| `Room` | `src/fastmdxplora/remote/gpu_room.py:106-128` | Aggregates workstation GPU states, active application bindings, and visibility scopes. |
| `Need` | `src/fastmdxplora/remote/gpu_room.py` | Encapsulates the projected VRAM requirement for a pending study execution. |

Sources: `src/fastmdxplora/remote/gpu_room.py:1-171`, `src/fastmdxplora/remote/send.py:21-30`

# Remote from the GUI

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

## Purpose and Scope
This page details the implementation of remote execution features within the FastMDXplora graphical user interface. It covers the HTTP routing layer managed by `RemoteDesk` (`[src/fastmdxplora/gui/remote_routes.py:1-20]()`), the cryptographic planning and safety constraints (`[src/fastmdxplora/gui/remote_routes.py:42-49](), [src/fastmdxplora/remote/inputs.py:1-32]()`), the client-side state machine and UI logic in `remote.js` (`[src/fastmdxplora/gui/static/remote.js:1-12]()`), and the corresponding CSS styling (`[src/fastmdxplora/gui/static/remote.css:1-13]()`). These components allow users to inspect recorded machines, plan transmissions, execute remote studies, track telemetry, and fetch or cancel jobs safely directly from the browser dashboard.

---

## 1. RemoteDesk Server Routing and API Endpoints

The GUI exposes remote capabilities through dedicated HTTP routes grouped under `/api/remote/`. These routes mirror the functionality of the `fastmdx remote` CLI command while enforcing strict security rules: loopback access only, host/origin validation, and complete disablement in hosted/cloud deployment modes (`[src/fastmdxplora/gui/remote_routes.py:1-20]()`).

### Route Tables and Handlers
The API is split into GET and POST endpoints defined in `RemoteDesk` (`[src/fastmdxplora/gui/remote_routes.py:108-112]()`):

| HTTP Method | Endpoint | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `GET` | `/api/remote/machines` | Lists recorded remote machines and active remote jobs (`[src/fastmdxplora/gui/remote_routes.py:109]()`). |
| `GET` | `/api/remote/job` | Queries the current status of a specific remote job. |
| `GET` | `/api/remote/fetch-sizes` | Calculates sizes of remote result artifacts prior to retrieval (`[src/fastmdxplora/gui/remote_routes.py:109]()`). |
| `POST` | `/api/remote/plan` | Generates a cryptographically bound transmission plan and token (`[src/fastmdxplora/gui/remote_routes.py:110]()`). |
| `POST` | `/api/remote/send` | Executes the transfer and starts the remote job using an active plan token (`[src/fastmdxplora/gui/remote_routes.py:110]()`). |
| `POST` | `/api/remote/forget` | Removes a completed or abandoned job record from dashboard tracking (`[src/fastmdxplora/gui/remote_routes.py:110-111]()`). |
| `POST` | `/api/remote/fetch` | Downloads completed results from the remote machine (`[src/fastmdxplora/gui/remote_routes.py:111]()`). |
| `POST` | `/api/remote/cancel` | Requests termination of a running remote job (`[src/fastmdxplora/gui/remote_routes.py:112]()`). |

Hosted environments (`_HOSTED`) explicitly reject all remote control mutations with a standard refusal payload (`[src/fastmdxplora/gui/remote_routes.py:114-115]()`).

Sources: `[src/fastmdxplora/gui/remote_routes.py:1-115]()`, `[tests/test_the_gui_reaches_your_machines.py:68-119]()`

---

## 2. Planning, Input Safety, and Cryptographic Binding

To prevent accidental transmission of sensitive files (such as SSH keys or credentials) and ensure the user's explicit consent matches exact file contents, remote transmissions follow a strict Plan-Send protocol.

### The `_Plan` Dataclass and Expiration
When a user clicks "Plan the send", the backend validates the configuration file path, checks workspace boundaries, computes file hashes, and issues an ephemeral `_Plan` object (`[src/fastmdxplora/gui/remote_routes.py:42-49]()`):

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["ClientPOST:/api/remote/plan"] --> B["RemoteDesk"]
    B --> C["_read_whole"]
    C --> D["_sha_of"]
    D --> E["_Plan"]
    E --> F["ReturnTokenAndDetails"]

    sub-class["Code Entities"]
    style sub-class fill:none,stroke:none
```
*Figure 1: Plan Generation Control Flow linking API entry points to `_Plan` generation.*

Plans are valid for a limited window (`PLAN_KEPT_S = 600` seconds) and can be redeemed exactly once (`[src/fastmdxplora/gui/remote_routes.py:35-36]()`, `[tests/test_the_gui_reaches_your_machines.py:111-143]()`).

### Input Security and Boundary Enforcement
Input collection (`[src/fastmdxplora/remote/inputs.py:1-32]()`) restricts files that can travel:
- Only files within the study's local folder are permitted.
- Symbolic links pointing outside the workspace or back into it are strictly blocked (`[src/fastmdxplora/remote/inputs.py:17-23]()`).
- Sensitive credential paths (`.ssh`, `.gnupg`, `.aws`) trigger hard refusals via `_through_keys` (`[src/fastmdxplora/gui/remote_routes.py:193]()`).
- File contents are verified via `_read_whole` using non-blocking, non-following descriptors (`[src/fastmdxplora/gui/remote_routes.py:51-80]()`).

Sources: `[src/fastmdxplora/gui/remote_routes.py:42-103]()`, `[src/fastmdxplora/remote/inputs.py:1-51]()`, `[tests/test_a_send_is_bound_to_what_travels.py:25-57]()`

---

## 3. Frontend Architecture (`remote.js`) and UI Styling (`remote.css`)

The dashboard user interface is driven by `src/fastmdxplora/gui/static/remote.js` (`[src/fastmdxplora/gui/static/remote.js:1-12]()`), which manages asynchronous API polling, DOM manipulation for the Config Builder, and job listings on the All Studies page.

### Client-Side State and Polling
`remote.js` maintains global lists of `machines` and `jobs`, alongside busy states (`busy`) to prevent redundant rendering during network latency (`[src/fastmdxplora/gui/static/remote.js:53-60]()`). Network requests are handled through a generalized `ask()` helper function (`[src/fastmdxplora/gui/static/remote.js:38-51]()`):

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["machinesKnown()"] --> B["ask(GET,/api/remote/machines)"]
    B --> C["ParseJSONResponse"]
    C --> D["renderRunOn()"]
    D --> E["UpdateDOMDropdowns"]

    sub-class["Code Entities"]
    style sub-class fill:none,stroke:none
```
*Figure 2: Frontend Data Synchronization Loop mapping `machinesKnown` to DOM updates.*

### DOM Integration in the Config Builder
The script positions the remote execution panel (`#run-remote`) either beneath the configuration file field or inside the actions card depending on whether the user is running an existing config file or building one interactively (`[src/fastmdxplora/gui/static/remote.js:111-129]()`). 

Remote jobs display dynamic status badges styled via `src/fastmdxplora/gui/static/remote.css`:
- `.remote-job-state[data-state="running"]` / `ready` (`[src/fastmdxplora/gui/static/remote.css:37-38]()`)
- `.remote-job-state[data-state="done"]` (`[src/fastmdxplora/gui/static/remote.css:39]()`)
- `.remote-job-state[data-state="failed"]` (`[src/fastmdxplora/gui/static/remote.css:40]()`)
- `.remote-job-state[data-state="abandoned"]` (`[src/fastmdxplora/gui/static/remote.css:41]()`)

Sources: `[src/fastmdxplora/gui/static/remote.js:38-175]()`, `[src/fastmdxplora/gui/static/remote.css:1-44]()`, `[tests/test_your_machines_on_the_page.py:83-125]()`

## Purpose and Scope

FastMDXplora ensures scientific rigour, reproducible outcomes, and code reliability through a multi-layered infrastructure combining automated test suites, pre-registered validation frameworks, strict continuous integration (CI) pipelines, and developer tooling. Rather than relying solely on passing unit tests, the system verifies behavior against independent implementations, guardrail corpora, and documented command examples.

For detailed technical implementation, refer to the child pages:
- [Test Suite Organisation](#7.1)
- [Scientific Validation, Corpus and Preregistration](#7.2)
- [CI, Packaging, Scripts and Contributing](#7.3)

---

## 7.1 Test Suite Organisation

The test suite is structured around behavior-named assertions, session-scoped fixtures, and validation of documented command-line examples. Tests are configured via `pytest` and decoupled into unit tests, network-dependent corpus checks, and integration tests covering CLI parsing and configuration loading.

To prevent documentation drift, command examples and markdown snippets are parsed and verified directly by test harnesses such as `tests/test_docs_examples.py`. Session-scoped preparation fixtures like those in `tests/validation/conftest.py` ensure that expensive PDB fetching and system setup operations run once per session, supplying consistent objects to downstream assertions.

### Diagram: Test Suite Mapping (Natural Language Space to Code Entity Space)

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph NaturalLanguageSpace["Natural Language Space"]
        A["Documented CLI Commands"] --> B["Command-Line Parser Check"]
        C["Setup & Preparation Fixtures"] --> D["Session-Scoped PDB Caching"]
        E["Agent Evaluation Registration"] --> F["Agent Turn & Tool Judging"]
    end

    subgraph CodeEntitySpace["Code Entity Space"]
        B --> G["tests/test_docs_examples.py:test_documented_fastmdx_commands_parse"]
        D --> H["tests/validation/conftest.py:prepared"]
        F --> I["src/fastmdxplora/validation/agent_eval.py:run"]
    end
```

**Sources:** `tests/test_docs_examples.py:1-67`, `tests/validation/conftest.py:65-150`, `src/fastmdxplora/validation/agent_eval.py:1-71`

For detailed configuration files, conftest fixtures, Playwright browser tests, and dependency-declaration checks, see [Test Suite Organisation](#7.1).

---

## 7.2 Scientific Validation, Corpus and Preregistration

Scientific validation goes beyond standard code testing by measuring rates, cross-tool comparisons, and agent behavior against pre-registered criteria. The `fastmdxplora.validation` package provides guardrail corpora (`DEFECTS` and `CLEAN`) to evaluate system refusals, cross-tool checks against independent packages like ProLIF and MDAnalysis (`docs/validation.md`), and environment consistency checks using `resolved_config.yml`.

The natural-language agent is judged by a pre-registered evaluation set (`preregistration/agent-eval-v2.md`) implemented in `src/fastmdxplora/validation/agent_eval.py`. This harness tests multi-turn conversations, repairs, edits, and documentation lookups without relying on ad-hoc adjustments.

### Diagram: Validation Pipeline (Scientific & Agent Metrics to Source Modules)

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph NaturalLanguageSpace["Natural Language Space"]
        V1["Guardrail Corpus Defect/Clean Checks"] --> W1["Refusal Calibration"]
        V2["Agent Evaluation Set (v2)"] --> W2["Multi-Turn Conversation Judging"]
        V3["Cross-Tool Independent Observables"] --> W3["MDAnalysis & ProLIF Comparison"]
    end

    subgraph CodeEntitySpace["Code Entity Space"]
        W1 --> X1["fastmdxplora.validation.corpus"]
        W2 --> X2["src/fastmdxplora/validation/agent_eval.py"]
        W3 --> X3["fastmdxplora.validation.cross_tool"]
        X2 --> Y1["preregistration/agent-eval-v2.md"]
    end
```

**Sources:** `docs/validation.md:1-125`, `src/fastmdxplora/validation/agent_eval.py:1-115`, `preregistration/agent-eval-v2.md:1-50`

For deep dives into cross-tool checks, agent evaluation harness mechanics, and preregistration documents, see [Scientific Validation, Corpus and Preregistration](#7.2).

---

## 7.3 CI, Packaging, Scripts and Contributing

FastMDXplora uses GitHub Actions workflows (`.github/workflows/tests.yml`) to govern multi-platform testing, scheduled corpus runs, and concurrency cancellation. Packaging constraints are strictly defined in `pyproject.toml`, managing optional dependencies like `[ligand]`, `[pdf]`, and `[validation]` while acknowledging packages requiring conda-forge distribution (such as `openff-toolkit` and `openmm-plumed`).

Developer utilities under `scripts/` provide smoke campaigns and measurement harnesses, aligning contributor contributions with the project's contribution workflow and dependency specifications (`docs/installation.md`).

### Diagram: CI and Packaging Workflow Architecture

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph NaturalLanguageSpace["Natural Language Space"]
        CI["GitHub Actions Tests & Schedules"] --> CW["Tests Workflow"]
        PKG["Dependency Management"] --> PY["pyproject.toml Metadata"]
        ENV["Environment Provisioning"] --> ML["environment.yml Conda Stack"]
    end

    subgraph CodeEntitySpace["Code Entity Space"]
        CW --> EX1[".github/workflows/tests.yml"]
        PY --> EX2["pyproject.toml"]
        ML --> EX3["environment.yml"]
    end
```

**Sources:** `.github/workflows/tests.yml:1-100`, `pyproject.toml:7-110`, `docs/installation.md:68-98`

For comprehensive details on GitHub workflows, container builds, shim-packages, and contributor guidelines, see [CI, Packaging, Scripts and Contributing](#7.3).

## Purpose and Scope
The FastMDXplora test suite is structured to prevent silent scientific and operational regressions. It enforces strict dependency tracking, state isolation between tests, automatic process termination for background tasks, and behavior-driven test naming. The suite verifies components across all layers: configuration schemas, setup pipelines, OpenMM-backed simulation runners, trajectory analyses, reporting generators, GUI servers, and AI agent endpoints.

Sources: `tests/conftest.py:1-16`, `pytest.ini:1-14` [pytest.ini:1-13](), [tests/conftest.py:1-16]()

---

## Pytest Configuration and Environment Isolation

Execution parameters are defined in `pytest.ini`, which mandates a strict 10-minute timeout per test using thread-based stack dumping to catch hanging CI runners [pytest.ini:4-8](). Custom markers distinguish network-dependent tests (`network`) from resource-intensive simulation runs (`slow`) [pytest.ini:9-11]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[""pytest.ini""] --> B[""addopts: -v --tb=short --timeout=600""]
    A --> C[""markers: network, slow""]
    A --> D[""testpaths: tests/""]
    E[""conftest.py""] --> F[""FASTMDXPLORA_CONFIG_DIR""]
    E --> G[""FASTMDXPLORA_CACHE_DIR""]
    
    classDef default stroke:#333,fill:#fff;
```
*Diagram 1: Test Suite Configuration and Environment Mapping*

Sources: `pytest.ini:1-14`, `tests/conftest.py:127-145` [pytest.ini:1-13](), [tests/conftest.py:127-145]()

---

## Shared Fixtures and State Management (`conftest.py`)

To prevent test cross-contamination, `tests/conftest.py` declares several autouse fixtures that reset logging configurations, clean up open matplotlib figures, terminate stray background runner processes, and isolate configuration/cache directories [tests/conftest.py:25-164]().

| Fixture Name | Scope | Role / Mechanism |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `_logging_state_is_restored` | Autouse | Restores `fastmdx` logger propagation levels and console handlers after each test [tests/conftest.py:25-63](). |
| `_a_test_closes_the_figures_it_opens` | Autouse | Closes any matplotlib figures left open during a test [tests/conftest.py:65-77](). |
| `_no_run_outlives_the_test_that_started_it` | Autouse | Wraps `DashboardRuntime._spawn()` to track and forcefully terminate child processes (`SIGTERM` / `SIGKILL`) upon test completion [tests/conftest.py:79-125](). |
| `pytest_configure` | Session | Directs configuration and cache paths to an isolated temporary directory (`FASTMDXPLORA_CONFIG_DIR`) [tests/conftest.py:127-145](). |
| `_this_computer_reads_no_gpu` | Autouse | Mocks `gpu_here.nvidia_smi_here()` to return `False`, ensuring deterministic multi-instance GPU sharing logic tests [tests/conftest.py:146-164](). |

Sources: `tests/conftest.py:25-164` [tests/conftest.py:25-164]()

---
